utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. This is Wednesday, and I welcome representatives from the Prosecution, our witness, Mr. Seselj, as well as everyone helping us. The cross-examination is going to continue and I will thus give the floor to Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, at the beginning of the examination-in-chief, you talked about the good pre-war relationships between the Serbs and Muslims in the Zvornik area and then you stated that the upset in the interethnic relations came about because of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences and their big plan; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said. That's my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What big plan is this of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can give you my opinion. Now whether it is correct or not, those are my conclusions nonetheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, give me your conclusions then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you put all the pieces of the puzzle together which I tried to do, and giving thought to how the situation came about in the first place, everything happened with the arrival of Dobrica Cosic, Vuk Draskovic, your own Bore Djordjevic and I'd link this up to the death of Branko Copic, his suicide. I was at school then but I think that this was on the news at the time that he convened a conference, a press conference at which he stated that a plan was being prepared for all non-Serbs to be killed after which he was proclaimed mad and he committed suicide. I think he jumped off a bridge, not into the water but on to the ground beside the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what year was this that Branko Copic committed suicide?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was 1985 or '86. 1986, I think, somewhere around there. I'm not quite sure so I couldn't give you those facts precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Several years before. But what press conference was it that he held with this plan, putting forward the plan that all non-Serbs be killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that a professor of Serbo Croatian at the time, my teacher, I had a lesson with him and I didn't know about politics at the time but I knew that he talked about us with that, that it was very sorry to see such a major writer go wrong and I remember him saying that. And I remembered his words several years later and I tried to link all this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you with every certainty that Branko Copic never convened any press conference before his suicide. He was persecuted under the Communist regime and suffered from paranoia. And when he had this depression, he jumped off Branko Radicevic Bridge, that was the name of the bridge. There was no conference so neither you nor the Prosecution can bring in a scrap of evidence to proof that Branko Copic held any press conference whatever, that's why I'm surprised by that statement of yours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was not certain, but, Mr. Seselj, what you are doing for 24 -- round the clock, you're dealing with things like this whereas I am not somebody who deals with the kind of work you deal with. I'm not a politician. I'm not an investigator; fourth, I'm not an attorney. I'm quite simply a man doing an ordinary job in order to survive, to have a livelihood and to take care of how I'm going to make ends meet to the end of the month and be able to look out for my family and feed it as best I can. So I don't think I have any leftover time for things like that but I just said that these were some of my thoughts. So I can't tell you about the facts. That is the way in which I put the puzzle together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, I have every sympathy with the problems you face in life and a lot of people live that way in the Balkans, most of them in fact so not only in your region, but everybody must be responsible for the words they utter so you must bear that in mind. So tell me now, please, where was it that Dobrica Cosic, Vuk Draskovic, Bore Djordjevic and I were taken into the Serbian academy? Is that where you mean when we were admitted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I don't know the dates when you became a member or not a member of the SANU, the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences. And as far as the academy goes, I said that I thought that's where it all began. So I didn't say that it did actually begin there, I said that I thought it began there and that according to my knowledge and information and what I had heard, read and seen, that's how things evolved, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you and tell me your views, that neither Vuk Draskovic nor Bore Djordjevic, nor I myself never became members of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences, not because we didn't wish to. Everybody wants to, every prominent intellectual in Serbia would like to become a member of the academy but there is such stringent criteria that we just didn't meet those criteria. So do you maintain that we actually became members of the Serbian academy, that we were admitted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I never said that. I said I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said you think we became members. Now, do you know that I was born in Bosnia too? Are you aware of that? I was born in Sarajevo, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that you were born in Bosnia but not where, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that we Bosnians, Serbs, Croats and Muslims, have -- I like to say that to think is one thing but to know is another. They are two quite different things; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you've heard about that proverb. I don't want to finish the proverb off. It's a national proverb but the second part isn't commensurate to things that we should say in court. So you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, have you ever heard about the Islamic declaration of Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about it. I have not read it ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But do you recall that the press wrote about it? That the press wrote about certain excerpts from that declaration among others, his position and view that life together between Muslims and non-Muslims in a single state was impossible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to repeat. I have never read the declaration myself. First, because before, writers wrote books. Today, everybody can write a book. So although this was written in our times, I haven't actually read it so I can't say what it says there. If that's what he wrote, then that's quite ludicrous because Muslims, Serbs and Croats for decades, for centuries lived together in Bosnia-Herzegovina without any major problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't without any greater problems through history, there were a lot of problems throughout history, let me remind you, Mr. VS-1013. Not everything was rosy because sometimes during the Turkish times, the Muslims were the privileged class and the Serbs and Croats were the underdogs, isn't that right? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really say. I didn't live during those times. I wasn't alive then so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you were taught history, you learned history at school, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did learn history.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What education do you have? Secondary school education or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So in primary school, elementary school, secondary school, you were taught history and you knew about the events that happened in the area. But yes, for several decades, there was a peaceful way of life, I agree with that. Now, do you know that in 1986, the authorities in Belgrade banned my book "The Witch-hunt for Heretics" by the court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that in the 1980s, I spoke about pan-Islamic tendencies and their appearance and emergence in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that I was tried in Sarajevo and given an eight-year prison sentence for hostile propaganda, or rather anti-Communist propaganda, Serb nationalism and other things which at that time under the Communist regime were incriminated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I read about that somewhere that you were in prison but that you were put on trial and why, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you don't really know anything about me except that I -- you say that I became a member of the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences. All right, Mr. VS-1013, tell me whether you know that already in 1991, under the auspices of the Party of Democratic Action, the so-called SDA, that was a party that rallied the largest number of Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that the so-called Patriotic League was formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That means you've never heard of the Patriotic League, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have heard of it when the war broke out. That's when I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And almost a year before the war, did you ever hear of a paramilitary organisation of the Patriotic League that was formed under the name of Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the Green Berets, I have heard of them. I think it was on television where they were shown. I don't know in all those pre-war settlings of account between the various nationalist parties it was mentioned a number of times. And on one occasion, I remember, I don't know what meeting it was but I remember that a man came out and said that these, I don't know, Green Berets existed and that he didn't know -- well, that they were rallying patriots because already at that time, if I can put it that way, there were intonations of a conflict looming and that they were ready to defend the country. Now, whether he said in the year -- or rather 2000 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2000 Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what was the basis, the main cause of the Serbian Muslim conflict at the end of the 1991 and the beginning of 1992? It was first of all a conflict between politicians and then it expanded to involve the general populous, the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what the basis of the conflict is, the reason for the conflict, well, I think that was an attempt to proclaim Bosnia-Herzegovina an independent state because with the disintegration of Yugoslavia quite simply all the republics or rather, Slovenia proclaimed its independence first followed by Croatia, and then the Bosnian and Herzegovinian politicians wanted to proclaim an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina too, and the Serbian Democratic Party which was the strongest party at the time was opposed to that and this led to heated arguments and discussions. I know that some of the meetings that were held went on until midnight and beyond and they were very heated statements, for instance by Karadzic who threatened that there would be no Muslims and Cengic who came out and made statements too. This was on television. He said don't let there be no Serbs. Anyway, the then politicians of Bosnia-Herzegovina behaved like children in kindergarten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's summarise this now. The Muslim and Croatian politicians wanted to see Bosnia-Herzegovina independent whereas the Serbian politicians wanted Bosnia-Herzegovina to remain within the composition of Yugoslavia; is that it? Would that be a summary of what you've just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's a summary because as far as I remember, and let me tell you quite frankly, I'm not an analyst of any kind, nor am I a political or military expert, but viewing the situation and these three parties, the SDA, the SDS and the HDZ, in a coalition form took over power from the Communists just to get rid of the Communists, you must be conscious of the fact that the Communists among their ranks had many Serbs, Croats, and Muslims so none of the nationalist parties in my opinion, I keep saying my opinion and as I see things because if I spoke of in the name of the state or state organs, well, I'm not such an important person and I don't have the education to do so and I don't think I'm intelligent enough to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS, I'm not underestimating you at all, Mr. VS-1013, not at all. I'm not underestimating you regardless of the fact that you haven't had any high education.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I say that to a large extent, they had a lot of people who came from all three ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's now go back to the Zvornik area. Is it true and correct that the first unrest and the first animosity that broke out between Serbs and Muslims in the Zvornik area took place when the question of and the dilemma came up of Bosnia's independence or should it remain within Yugoslavia? Is that where the rift began on a nationalist level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: An ethnic rift broke out in large part because of what you've said and also, little by little, there was a nationalist rift with the war in Croatia where certain ethnic groups had different positions and views vis-a-vis the war. Some of them said that the party that didn't want to live -- for example, your wife, if she didn't want to live with you, if she doesn't want to live with you and wants to divorce, you can't force her to continue living with you so that's my position too. If anybody doesn't wish to live with anybody else, you needn't do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not asking about your position but is it true that in 1991, for instance, the JNA conducted mobilisation in Bosnia and Herzegovina of the reserve force, the reservists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they conducted mobilisation. I know that certain people would be called up to report to the reserve formations and units and that some people fled abroad because of that and others went into hiding even. But that a general all-out mobilisation was conducted in 1991, I really don't know. I can't say. I wasn't in a position for me to be able to tell you that, whether it did or did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about mobilisation? Did it start at the beginning of 1992, then? Was there mobilisation in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mobilisation as such, I think that in the villages, for example around Zvornik, that the JNA did start to call people up to the reserve force or mobilise them, I don't know which term is best suited, and it did issue military kits to people and certain Serbs would tell their friends of many years standing that 15 to 20 days before the war that they went to do a military exercise and then went to work after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true and correct that when these people were called up for military training and partial mobilisation, because an all-out general mobilisation was never actually proclaimed before the war, is it true and correct that the Serbs almost regularly responded to the call-up whereas the Muslims avoided doing so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that the Serbs were indeed mobilised. Now whether the Muslims received call-ups for mobilisation, I'm not sure. I remember a few young guys who did receive call-ups in 1991 to join the reserve force and that they avoided doing so because they were afraid that they would be sent somewhere to the battle front in Croatia or wherever and I think this was in 1991. Now, whether in 1992 the Muslims received call-up papers, I don't know. I personally didn't receive any so I can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about the village of Donja Kamenica in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about Sahmani, a hamlet of that village? So, have you heard about the hamlet of Sahmani in that village, part of that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have heard about it. Sahmani, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you heard that in mid-March, 1992, a group of five Serb young men were arrested in this village and that this was the first major incident in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am not aware of that. As far as I know, to the best of my knowledge, the first incident occurred in the area around Sapna, I don't know where exactly, but I've not heard about this area of Sahmani, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This incident in Sahmani occurred in March and the Muslim village of Sapna in the Zvornik municipality, that's where the first murder occurred in the Zemun municipality. Do you know who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was a non--commissioned officer of the JNA Nika Stanojevic, he was a sergeant and several soldiers were wounded when their column came up against a roadblock in that village and fire was opened on them without any warning. And then when this sergeant or rather a warrant officer was killed, the troops returned fire and the Muslim, I think, was killed. I don't have his name. Have you heard about this incident, this conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about this clash, but because I was not there and neither were you, I could not really ascertain what really happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But do you agree that the first victim fell on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the interpreters are asking you to stop -- to turn off your mike once you have put your question and to turn it back on when you're asking your question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what I do most of the time, but sometimes I just forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear my question? Is this the first victim in this clash between Muslims and Serbs in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was shooting but as to who opened fire first, well, one Muslim was killed and one Serb. I couldn't then tell you this but I would say that these were the first two victims in this clash.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, well, on the same day, the first two victims of this conflict but the JNA approached as the regular armed force of Yugoslavia, and the local Muslims and their paramilitaries set up a roadblock and they opened fire. These are the facts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you how this occurred because I was not there. But I do know that at that time, roadblocks were set up by all and sundry, wherever they felt like and everybody would stop there, so I couldn't tell you how this clash actually occurred. Fortunately, I myself was never stopped at any roadblock because I am from Zvornik and I just moved around Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know who Sead Hadziavdic is, from Drinjaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He owns the Royal Cafe, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think the name of the cafe was Royal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the first to start procuring weapons in an organised manner for the illegal arming of the Muslims from his village and the OTP is in possession of a report from the state security service from Zvornik, from autumn 1991, where this is stated. Have you heard anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arming them? I heard that he was selling weapons, probably to arm people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, selling weapons. So procuring weapons and selling them to his fellow Muslims; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard but I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know who Saban Redzic from Kamenica is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know who Sead Haskic from Kamenica is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Saban Redzic sold weapons to his compatriots in Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know who Captain Almir is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What is his real name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would his real name be Samir Nistovic, could that be his real name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell you that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he the person who organised the Patriotic League and the Green Berets as its armed wing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you that. I know that when I fled to Kula, that there was a man up there who was shouting at people, beating them up and people were saying that this was Captain Almir but I didn't know him and I didn't really pay much attention to what he was saying because he was trying to organise some form of defence there. But now, as to whether there was any organisation that he set up or not, it is my opinion and that's the only thing that I can give you, he wouldn't be running around in complete -- completely upset running around from people telling them, Stop, stop, we have to defend this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But there is testimony that he was not a competent commander, but this is not at issue here but you do not, you do not contest that he was commanding the Muslim forces there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Muslim leadership in the Zvornik municipality raised the reserve force of the MUP, of the police, and provided arms to them as early as in January of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that the reserve force of the MUP was called up but not the Muslim part. But if I may say so, that was the Serb-Muslim force; there were reservists both of Serb and Muslim ethnic background. And after the roadblock was set up, as far as I can recall, some other people were admitted to this reserve force of the MUP after the Serb policemen left the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to the reports, local hoodlums joined the MUP, the reserve force. They bragged and walked around in their MUP uniforms and they were instilling fear both in Serbs and in Muslims; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. First of all because those hoodlums and thugs did join the force but that was only a day or two after the shooting, after the roadblock was set up. And they were strutting around, yes, that is true, and they were bragging, but as to whether they were instilling fear in Zvornik, I wouldn't agree with that. They were doing check-ups at the bridge leading in and out of Zvornik. They were searching everybody but as far as I know, they did not use any corrosive measures against anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear from Mithat Grahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never heard about Mithat Grahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is a local criminal from Zvornik who set up a unit called Dzamijski Golubovi, the Mosque Pigeons, does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the war I heard about the existence of this unit but I don't know this Mithat. I may know him by sight because Zvornik was not a big town, but as for his name, I can't remember him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But do you know that those Mosque Pigeons, before the war, were roaming around Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And have you heard about a paramilitary organisation called Cobras?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was set up by Sulejman Trsic. Before the war, he taught in the elementary school in Sapna.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Before the war, Sapna was part of the Zvornik municipality and after the war, now, it is part of the federation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know about a man by the name of Semsudin Muminovic, nicknamed Cobra? He later went on to become the commander of the Zvornik Brigade of the BH army, sometime late in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name sounds familiar but I don't know this man and I have not heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that the president of the municipality, and the SDA commissioner was Abdulah Pasic, a former dentist in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to correct you. He was not a dentist, it was Asim. He was the dentist. He was the president of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who was the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Pasic. I think he worked at the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. So now I have a little mistake here. Do you know who Nedjo Cahic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear his name mentioned. I think he was an active duty serviceman. I knew his brother, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was the commander of the municipal Territorial Defence staff and they took over the weapons from the depot of the Milicija and the Territorial Defence depots and they used those weapons to arm the Muslims on the eve of the 8th of April, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with you for one reason and that is the fact that -- or rather, as far as I know, I think that he came not to Zvornik but to Sapna or Tuzla but it was later and I don't recall him being in Zvornik before the war. And as for whether the weapons were taken out or not, I don't know that. The only thing I can say is that the JNA forces took the military files from the military department and also the weapons from the Territorial Defence depots. As far as I know, again, I stress, as far as I know, the only weapons that were at the disposal were those that were held by the reserve force of the police. As far as I know, the JNA members took the files and the weapons from the Territorial Defence with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know the HAP platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We who lived in Bosnia used the term Hapati, it's a slang term for stealing. That would be the kind of street language.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the street language, the slang.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And this HAP platoon was deployed to loot Serb villages, apartments, houses and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with you. Well, what does it mean to loot? I was not with them. But as far as I know, they were set up according to the information that I have, they were set up only once the lines were established so when some actions were carried out, they were in the position to steal some private property from Serb homes. But to say that they were roaming around Zvornik looting Serb property, you couldn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, nobody looted Serb property in Zvornik before the 8th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the property of the Serbs who left their homes and apartments and fled across the Drina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, this did not happen. There may have been some incidents, isolated incidents but I'm sure that there was no looting and all-out stealing from departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know who Himzo Tulic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Himzo Tulic was a well-known architect before the war in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He designed several buildings in Zvornik, a cultural hall, cultural centre, things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a surveyor. I don't know what kind of jobs he did but he had a master's degree in land survey.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was the public company in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that Himzo Tulic, once he left Zvornik, he went Austria or Germany or wherever, wrote a book entitled "Zvornicka Sirat-Cuprija." I have this book here with me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you do know about his book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that in this book, he describes the killing of Zvornik Muslims, prisoners, civilians, the suffering that those who fled went through and things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about that, but I, myself, don't like to revisit those events and experiences.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But, sir, VS-1013, you came here to evoke those memories of those ugly events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, and -- but it's very difficult for me and I'm trying to go back to my normal life.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you have to admit that I'm very fair towards you. I don't want to reopen any of your wounds, to go beyond what is my objective right in carrying out this cross-examination, for me to be able to establish some truth in all of this, do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This man, Himzo Tulic, at page 130 of his book mentions a certain number of Muslim paramilitary formations: The Cobras, the Mosque Pigeons, HAP platoon, the Drina Dragons, the Moce, and Mis from Goduce, the battalion and the mortar detachment. When have you heard of all those Muslim formations, have you heard about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I know it's difficult to remember, I have the same problem, but I would like to ask the accused to try to remember to turn off the microphone after he has put his questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought that the Prosecutor had some vital objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let me take this opportunity to say that you must pause between question and answer. You have a fairly loud voice, as you know, and then I cannot hear the translation into French. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Himzo Tulic says here that those units in June were linked up to set up to 206th Zvornik Brigade which was envisaged as the core of the future Drina Corps. Do you know that in June, this 206th Muslim Zvornik Brigade was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seselj, I don't know that because -- are you talking about 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. That's when you were in detention.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in detention then. Let me go back now. I heard about the existence of those units and now as to how they were set up and who was their commander in chief and so on, I don't know that because I was simply not there. I can tell you what I heard, rumours, what people were saying and what I read in the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, very well, I understand you fully. Now, let's look at this Sejtan legion and "Sejtan" means devil in Arabic or Turkish; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Sejtan, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it's the Devil's Legion, right, translated into Serbian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. I just want us to clarify certain things. What is completely understandable to you and me need not be clear to the judges, so I'm trying to clarify things. Now, Himzo Tulic in this book of his describes the events before the war and the rift in the SDA party, that is the main Muslim party and he was in the Muslim Bosniak organisation and as a critic from outside, he spoke about this rift. Now, do you know that in the SDA, there was indeed a rift before the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I never delved in politics so there is always a power struggle but if he writes about that since he dealt with matters of that kind, then that must be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, he says on page 15 for instance, that the executive board of the party became divided as he says into two almost equal factions, one more liberal than the other, rallied around the president of the municipality, Pasic, Jasim Hadzic and the other more conservative faction rallied around the Juzbasic, and both of these sides or parties considered themselves to be the legitimate representatives of the Muslim people. And the main board of the SDA attempted on several occasions to have them resolve their differences through an emissary but was unsuccessful. And instead of them settling their differences, the conflicts increased and assemblies were called to replace various people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he says so, then it must be correct, although I tell you that I didn't know about things like that but since he was a politician and dealt with politics then that must have been correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Himzo Tulic is a highly respected man in Zvornik, he's a prominent citizen and wouldn't take lightly to lying about things like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, politics is a tricky business, Mr. Seselj. Probably what he says is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He goes on to say that these conflicts engulfed the SDA membership and then he explains the causes of the Muslim defeat with the 8th of April because he said that the president of the municipality and the commander of the Territorial Defence fled from Zvornik and so on and so forth, but we're not going to dwell on the details there now. What I'm interested in this regard is this: And I can offer it up for the overhead projector, perhaps. Can we place it on the ELMO? When it comes to arming, just a paragraph, so that we can read it out to bring things home. I'm not the only person who reads this book and I'm quite sure that The Hague OTP has the book too. Let's just place that paragraph on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not going to object to the use of the book the way it's being used now, but I would place on the record that we have not been notified of the accused's intention to use any documents in cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you want to read it out or shall I read the first marked paragraph out? I'll read it out, if you find that more acceptable. "Just prior to the war, at this first and last meeting of the Crisis Staff" and it's the municipal Crisis Staff that he's talking about that the SDA formed, "One side did its utmost to prove to the other that it had armed its people." So you have two sides amongst the Muslims themselves and they are entering into a race and say how they armed their own people. And the SDS, if it begins this war, will have no chance at all, even if the JNA joins them. The lies were so convincing that most of the people believed them, which was a catastrophe. The people should not have been lied to. Instead of that, plans of evacuation for the population to leave town and the settlement in the Drina valley should have been designed had that been done, the overall balance of war crimes in our area would certainly have been different. Now, could you give the book back to me. Now, from the Muslim aspect, Himzo Tulic is explaining the situation from the Muslim aspect and says that among this Muslim leadership where there was a rift, each side boasted who had managed to supply more weapons and be better organised; however, when armed conflict and armed settling of accounts took place, a defeat ensued, almost in a single day. Have I interpreted this properly, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says so, yes, you've interpreted it correctly, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we have listened carefully to this excerpt being read out. This was authored by a prominent figure in Zvornik, a Muslim person. The author of this book says that there was a rift within the SDA but the author also says that there was arming on the part of the Muslims. And I connect this sentence with what you told us yesterday. Yesterday, you told us, "I bought a Kalashnikov," so I would like to spell this out and I want this to be cleared up. You bought it as part of the arming of the Muslim population, as is recounted by the author of this book or you bought this weapon personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I bought it, actually, on my neighbour's advice, and I didn't purchase it through these parties, but the man took me to see another man. He sold these on the black market. He was a black marketeer in a village. I don't remember the village's name. Just let me take a moment to try to remember what it was called. I think the name of the village was Sopotnik. And I think that the man had nothing to do with the parties. I think quite simply -- well, I didn't actually know him. I stayed in the car, in my neighbour's car until he settled the deal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling us the truth when you say it's not you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: About a week prior to the beginning of the conflict which was on the 8th of April, it appeared as if the SDA leadership had settled its differences. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says in the book, then probably that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you know that on the 7th of April, the day before the conflict, there were negotiations between the Serbs and Muslims attended by municipal representatives of the SDA and SDS parties. The Muslims were represented by Pasic and Pezerovic and the Serbs were represented as it says here in Tulic's book by Grujic and Ivanovic. Now the JNA was represented by a colonel of the tank unit by the name of Tadic. Have you ever heard of these negotiations on the 7th of April between the Serbs and the Muslims which were attended by JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that at the time the representatives of the Serbian and Muslim Crisis Staffs achieved some sort of agreement, three-point agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that news was broadcast that some agreement had been reached but what it was about, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. If you don't know the contents of the agreement, we won't go into that. But anyway, the essence of the matter was that the authorisations in Zvornik municipality be divided up, that police control be divided up, according to settlements where the Serbs were in the majority or where the Muslims were the majority population, that was the essence of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard that there was some agreement but what they agreed upon, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, let's see what the problem was there. After this agreement had been reached, Himzo Tulic on page 20 states the following. Do you want me to place that on the overhead projector, if the Trial Chamber would like to see it on the ELMO; if not, I'll just read it out, read the excerpt out. It's to be found on page 20, paragraph 3 and it says, "That same night, there was a putsch in the SDA Crisis Staff, that is to say in the Muslim party, and a conciliation of the two conflicting parties did not last a week. And a Turkish word "hefta" is used, it's a Turkish word. Those of us who lived there know that it means "week." And Dedic Nezir, a reserve major, is placed to head the staff and after taking stock of the military situation, the new commander proposes an agreement. After this, the Crisis Staff disintegrated, some of the members of the staff left the town and fled and some of them joined the Crisis Staff at Kula Grad. So that was the night before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether that was so, I'm not sure, Mr. Seselj. I don't know. The man who wrote that, I know him and I have a high opinion of him. Now whether that was as he describes it, well, it's his own opinion. We would have to hear the other side for me to be able to see that that was it, 100 per cent. We can only go by what he wrote. I have a high regard for him but I would prefer hearing two or three opinions. I don't doubt his writings but I can't say that that's actually how it was because I wasn't there. I wasn't a political representative of the SDA or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. I won't trouble you with Himzo Tulic's book anymore. It was important for me for us to review the situation in Zvornik prior to the outbreak of the conflict of the 8th of April. We have seen how Tulic describes it and he says that there was disorganisation amongst the Muslims, mutual conflicts, and that because of that, they were defeated on the 8th of April, the day after they violated the agreement with the Serb representatives in the JNA. Now, the fight for Zvornik did not last long, for the town itself, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what was agreed and secondly, I don't know who violated the agreement. But the battles for the town did not last long. I think that already by nightfall, the Serbs had control of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, the fighting for Kula Grad went on longer and Kula Grad is a fortress, a large fortress above Zvornik, and then there is a Muslim village that follows on from the fortress also called Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the fortress is in a good strategic position and during Turkish times it was considered to be invincible; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it has got a good strategic position, whether it was considered invincible, I don't know, I haven't heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The firing from the tanks could do nothing to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it was only infantry fighting that could take place to take control of Kula Grad and the fighting went on for days, that is to say, from the 8th of April, as the day of the conflict in Zvornik, right up until the 26th of April. Now, the 26th of April, which was the Orthodox religious holiday when Kula Grad fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did fall. There was shooting from the direction of Kula Grad. Now, what the fighting was and what happened, how it was conducted, I can't say, but it is true that it was on Easter day that Kula fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you happened to be there somewhere at Kula Grad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there the day before it fell, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were there stand guard at some post, I can see that from your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not engaged at all. I didn't have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm not holding you for responsible for that. There was a civil war. I'm not accusing anybody of bearing weapons. I'm just accusing people who committed crimes. So you don't have to have this defensive attitude. Anyway, Mr. VS-1013, do you know which forces --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were saying that in Kula Grad while the fighting was going on, you had no weapon. Where was the weapon you'd bought? You buy a weapon which you don't use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The first day I had the weapon with me. The next morning when I woke up, my father told me that we had to go in the direction of Tuzla and I still had it with me. I got in the car with it but he said, "Get out of the car." He seized it from me. People were passing by, and he gave it to someone passing by. And I said, "Wait a minute. Let me give it to someone I know at least." And a young guy came by whom I knew from the cafe and so I gave the weapon to him. And then he took him with me, we moved off in the direction of Tuzla, we took a turn, and went to a village which wasn't far from Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There's another book here that I'd like to mention. I haven't got it in front of me but I have a quotation from the book. Have you ever heard of Besim Ibisevic who was the president of the municipality of Srebrenica in February 1991 and April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He is a historian by profession and he published a book called "Srebrenica from 1987 to 1992" in Amsterdam. It was printed in 1999. I'm sure the OTP has the book. I haven't managed to get a copy of the original but the OTP can, but there is a very characteristic quotation from the book and it to be found on pages 64 and 65 where he says the following: "In the second half of 1990, in Nova Kasaba, a cafe called Jugum [phoen] a meeting was held of the representatives of the SDA of Zvornik, Bratunac, Srebrenica, Vlasenica, Visegrad, Kalesija, and Rogatica. Presiding over the meeting was Mehmed Kavazbasic from Vlasenica, and on behalf of the SDA's central office, Izmet Kasumovic was present. It was agreed that weapons should be supplied for the Muslims and setting up guards as well and look into the possibility of toppling the bridge over the Drina and cutting off the roads and communication lines towards Serbia." Have you heard anything about that ever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This same author, Besim Ibisevic, on page 159 writes as follows, he says: "At the beginning of February 1992, a meeting was held of the representatives of the SDA of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Zvornik, and Vlasenica. The meeting was held at Mount Susica in a hunting hut there, that's Srebrenica municipality. The topic of the meeting was preparations for the war." That is to be found on page 159, have you heard of that meeting in February 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know, since you were at Kula Grad at the time when it fell, what units from the Serb side participated in the attack at Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that because I was just running away helter-skelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I will tell you, according to my knowledge what units participated in this attack and then you can confirm whether you know about it or not. Do you agree with that approach?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the Serb side, it was the special unit of the JNA from Pancevo. About 100 volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. One of Arkan's units participated, I don't know their strength, and a group of the reserve or the wartime force of the police from Zvornik also participated and it was joined by a group of volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party from Loznica and this whole unit was under the command of an active-duty police officer, Mr. Jekic, Vojislav Jekic. Have you ever heard of Vojislav Jekic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. So when I tell you now who participated in the attack on Kula Grad to my knowledge, do you have any objections and remarks, do you have anything to deny or to confirm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not hear who participated in the attack. I do know that on one occasion, when we were being guarded at Ciglana that one of the guards said to another, he was wearing the military police uniform, he said that he had participated in the attack on Kula Grad and that his weapon had jammed and that he had been really scared. He hadn't known what to do. A military police officer said that so this is the only thing that I can tell you about the units that had participated in this attack and about this man who led them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's just understand one thing. You're talking about the military policemen. On the 26th of April, the military police did not participate in the attack but there are previous attacks on Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so. You could hear shots from that direction every day, not very intense but sometimes it was sporadic but we could hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But there was some failed attacks on Kula Grad; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. At least that's what the story is heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear about Arkan's attempts to take Kula Grad and some of his best fighters got killed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that his brother-in-law got killed or maybe his best fighter, I don't know. As far as I heard from the stories, they tried to infiltrate the town, and they started a conflict there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This person was Rambo, the guy who got killed as his best fighter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that was a few days before the final attack on Kula Grad that I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Kalesija which is the neighbouring municipality in the direction of Tuzla fell before Kula Grad actually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Kalesija is the municipality neighbouring Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Muslims and Serbs live in Kalesija but the majority of them are Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Kalesija, for a month, was under the Serb control which was in April up to the 11th of May or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that. I was not aware of the exact dates, but I know that one time while we were still in Ciglana, people came from the direction of Kalesija because I suppose that the Patriotic League Force, as they were known at the time, had taken Kalesija again and the guards told us, "We will come back from Kalesija."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you didn't know who participated in the attack on Kula Grad but if I tell you that a special unit of the JNA from Pancevo and the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party returned immediately to Serbia as soon as Kula Grad fell, what would you say about that? Am I telling the truth or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you. I wasn't there. How many members of the Serbian Radical Party were there and from which municipalities, I wouldn't be able to tell you either. I only know that people from Kraljevo that guarded us later on were there. Whether they participated in the attack on Kula Grad or not, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I can only tell you that people from Kraljevo did not participate in Kula Grad but we will discuss that a bit later. Now we will come to your statement that you provided in Vienna in 1993 to the representatives of the Muslim authorities. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Representatives of the Muslim authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993? No, I provided a statement in 1996 to the Hague Tribunal. Some people came, some people wrote statements and asked for my statement, but the only official statement that I have provided was in 1996 to The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this statement please be displayed on the ELMO, but in private so that the identity of this witness will not be revealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... going to decide among ourselves whether we are going to move into private session for this part.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I insist that this should not be in closed session. I'm not going to do anything that might reveal this witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. We're going to have a look at the document. Could you give us the document first so that we see it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is number 00301430 that I was given by the Prosecutor. I can provide it to you but I think it would be in order for the Prosecutor to provide you with the document. I received it last week from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor gave you the document but I don't have it. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, are you aware of this document? Do you know it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, we have disclosed this document to the accused. It is for the accused to prepare his cross-examination and come with the copies and the documents he needs to use. It's not for the Prosecution to be his case manager. I don't know if we have a spare copy that we can bring. I'm sure that we can look into that now. It is my understanding that it is technically possible to show the document just in the courtroom. So as long as the accused's questions do not reveal the identity of the witness, we probably don't need to go into private session if the accused prefers to be in open session. But of course he has to put questions which don't reveal the identity of the witness but that's a general rule that doesn't only apply to this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we can put the document on the ELMO as long as this is not shown outside this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, last year, I was informed through the e-court that I am supposed to give only the ERN number and that the registry is able to display the document on the screen, so I have adapted to the system. Could you please put this on the ELMO without the general public being able to see. You're just going to show -- we are going to show the whole page, all three of them. We will go through the entire document. We will display all the three pages of this document. Now, what channel will this be displayed on for me? Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, can you see your name here, the date of birth, the address, the occupation and the passport number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you please go to page 3 for the gentleman to see his signature and to confirm whether this is his authentic signature or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the date when you provided this statement in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see the name of the person who took the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This person took the statement on behalf of the Muslim authorities in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I must tell you something. I've been providing all sorts of statements. I was not looking at the date, but I suppose that is that. I know that my first official statement was taken in 1996 for The Hague Tribunal and on behalf of The Hague Tribunal, but I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I am glad that you recognised the signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you are not contesting that this is your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please, can we slowly go across the first, second and third pages. I would like to show you that nowhere in this statement did you mention members of the Seselj group, you don't mention my name or the Serb Radical Party. Let's start looking at the text. Could you please start moving the text, madam, towards the top and let's see if Seselj's men are mentioned anywhere. Let's move on. Go to the next page please. Start at the top, please. Scroll towards the bottom. Go on. Go on. Are you able to follow or is this too fast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's go to page 3 now. Start from the top and move towards the bottom of the page. Have you managed to have a good look? Is it correct that you don't mention Seselj's men, that you don't mention my name or the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, that's correct. But I did mention certain members of your party, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We will look into that. We will see whether they really belong to the party or not. You mentioned people under their nicknames, this concurs with your subsequent statements and these are people of whom you said that they tortured detainees, both the members of the military and civilians and I'm not contesting any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be allowed to look at the statement, because I think he's going too fast for him to look at. It says on, I believe it's page 3 of the statement, and I'm reading from the English translation that I have, for example, it says: "On one occasion, a Djuk from Karlovac visited us, a general Chetnik," and so on and so forth. And there's more references to Chetnik so I think the witness should be allowed to look at the statement before the questions are being put to him in this way and he's being asked to confirmed what groups he has mentioned or not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can wait for as long as it takes, but please do not take this into account as the time for my cross-examination. And I would like to draw attention to the fact that Seselj's men are one thing and Chetniks are another thing. Croats and Muslims refer to everybody as Chetniks even the JNA. I'm not contesting the fact that he is mentioning Chetniks and Vojvoda from Karlovac, what were the -- how should I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you need more time to peruse the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What Mr. Seselj asked me about the Serb Radical Party, it is not mentioned here at all. What is being mentioned is Vojvoda from Kraljevo, the true Chetnik with long hair and long beard. I am mentioning names and nicknames but as for what Mr. Seselj asked me about the Serb Radical Party, this is not mentioned here. Chetniks are mentioned on several occasions and in several paragraphs, but I have not mentioned the SRS here or at least the lady who took a note of my statement did not take it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you are not mentioning Seselj's name, there is no my name, there is no reference to any of those here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, no reference of that is made here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Can we have the document again. I would like to see the date of the document on the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the last page, page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have questions, but I shall first give the floor to Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is your most recent statement after all that you went through and the sufferings that you experienced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one today?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, the one that you are looking at now. Could you please bring that paper over to me? This was provided only a year after you suffered through the detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then your memory was the freshest, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was much fresher than it is today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in 1996, when you provided your statement to the OTP of The Hague Tribunal, you mentioned Seselj's men on several occasions. Who talked to you in Sarajevo before you met with the investigators of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who contacted you from the AID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know what AID, the Muslim secret service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't know what AID is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In that case, I won't ask you anything. I am astonished that you don't know who AID is or what the organisation is, but it was suggested to you to mention Seselj in 1996. I've tried to locate this Vojvoda Celo, this is the person you mentioned in your first question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cele.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the first statement you said Celo, the statement Vienna. I tried to find a photo, I managed it in Himzo Tulic's book, I found a photo of a person with long hair who tortures a Muslim prisoner; one of them is covered in blood. I'm going to show you the photo. It depicts a person from the back. I would like to know and hear from you when you look at the hair and the height and the picture of the person, would you be able to recognise this person this Vojvoda Cele that you spoke about? Could you please put this photo on the ELMO. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have not been given a copy of this or notified that the accused was going to use this. Your Honours have ordered that the accused provide us with a notification of a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lower this down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- he hasn't done that. I object to this line of cross-examination. I could have pulled in random photographs and used that and I refrained from doing that. I am opposed to the use of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, there are rules that have been set out by way of a decision issued by the Trial Chamber. When, for the sake of the cross-examination, the accused produces documents, he has to disclose the documents prior to the beginning of the cross-examination. The documents have to be disclosed to the Prosecution and to the Trial Chamber. I can very well understand that you are physically in a difficult situation, you are alone and you have to manage a whole host of events. Therefore, this objection is sustainable but one has to factor in as well certain specific circumstances. This objection pertains to the photograph that is to be found in this book. This is a book that exists, it was not invented for this purpose here. It has some relevance, that's the least we can say. Now, as to the probative value, we'll see later. There is a photograph, I can see some individuals in it. Obviously one of them has been hit if not tortured and there is an individual who is looking at them. And it seems that the question the accused wants to put to you is whether this individual whom we can see, we can see his hair and his stature, and he wants to know whether this is the famous Vojvoda Cele. I'm going to ask my colleagues what they think of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the interest of justice, the Trial Chamber is going to allow the accused to show this photograph and to put a question about what we can see in this photograph. Put your question, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I know that it is difficult to identify somebody from the back, but on the basis of this long hair, the typical hat that you can see on this person's head, you can see the knife at this person's belt at the left-hand side. I don't know what else could be characteristic, but could this be the person that you identified as Vojvoda Celo from Kraljevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. Could you please hand me the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This morning, I gave 7 pages of documents to be photocopied for the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution. I would like to use those documents after the break. I assume that there will be a break in five or six minutes. Please give this back to me. I hope that the Prosecution will have enough time to study those documents. I obtained those documents yesterday and I was not in a position to hand them over sooner and I will be using them in the cross-examination of this witness. I would like to make a remark regarding what I said yesterday. I was able to learn that the questioning of Miroslav Vukovic, Cele, as a suspect, was done by Mr. Mussemeyer, who appeared in this courtroom on several occasions. It is -- this statement is very important for me in this cross-examination. I learned some facts that I had not known before, that at the time, Miroslav Vukovic, Cele, was in contact with Ljubisa Petkovic, that he went to Zvornik from Banja Junakovic where he had been undergoing treatment, and that he was there to guard and secure the Glinica Factory. This statement is valuable to me and I'm not in a position in use it now because the Prosecution did not hand it over, did not disclose it because they are trying to cover everything up. If Mr. Mussemeyer was here, he would be able to give us some details. I'm not in a position to know everything, to know all the details that occurred during the war but this is why there is this voluminous documentation and I'm trying to use it. In this statement, there are some very important details and since we will be unable to use it with this witness, it would be essential for us to use it in the examination of future witnesses, but to do so, we will have to get an official translation. I hope that I will get a statement from Miroslav Vukovic, Cele, himself. It will be a brief statement, just a summary, but he did provide a long statement to the OTP several years ago. So if you are in a position to order the OTP to obtain this statement, I would be very grateful to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I have listened to the accused and it appears that Miroslav Vukovic, aka Cele, from what Mr. Seselj has, in terms of information, but he has so much information that sometimes we are astounded that he should be aware of so many things. Well, this Miroslav Vukovic, apparently, was interviewed by your own associate whom we had the pleasure of seeing here on several occasions in this courtroom. Yesterday, I was delving into your pre-trial brief which I still have in front of me. Page 43, footnote 284, mention is made of this Cele and still in the pre-trial brief, page 44, footnote 309, this Cele is mentioned again. So how is it that an individual who is in support of your case in your pre-trial brief has been heard by the OTP? How is it that his statement was not disclosed to the accused? I'm not challenging you, because you took up this case at the last minute, but this is a real question. How is it that somebody who is mentioned in a pre-trial brief in a footnote in support of the arguments being tried in the indictment, who was heard by the OTP, how is it that his statement was not disclosed to the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Thank you for the floor. The interview of this individual was taped. My understanding is that again, it's a situation where, as we attempted to disclose the recorded interview, the accused refused to accept it. We do have English transcripts. We are working on translating those transcripts into B/C/S and they will be disclosed as soon as they are available. It's -- much of this, Your Honour, comes down to the simple issue of resources and as each -- with respect to each indication of something else becoming a top priority, other things necessarily have to be reevaluated. There is a huge back-log of material, transcripts, Rule 68 material, suspect interviews, interviews mentioning the accused by name, all of this material, pursuant to the Chamber's orders, must be translated into Serbian and there is simply a huge backlog of material that needs to be either transcribed or transcribed and translated into B/C/S. So the bottom-line answer is we have an English transcript, we have tape recordings of these interviews but neither of those are acceptable to the accused and as a result he will get the material as soon as it's available. At some point, Your Honours, we very well may face the crisis situation where we simply will need to adjourn this hearing in order to produce the material in the Serbian language for the accused. I don't think we're at that point yet but I do and will continue to stress that there are certain logistical and human resource limitations upon us and we are providing this material as quickly as we possibly can. I don't believe that this individual is listed on the Prosecution's witness list, although I do acknowledge that there are references to him in the Prosecution pre-trial brief.
