But again, it's a question of simply having the resources to translate and transcribe all of this material into the Serbian language in light of the accused's refusal to accept transcripts in English or tape recordings which are in both English and Serbian. Obviously these interviews were conducted in both languages so that the Serbian language is audible on the tapes, but we simply can't transcribe and translate this material quickly enough in order to forestall each and every possible scenario of which material Dr. Seselj says he wants today versus something that can be provided next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Prosecutor has provided an answer and I have no comment on this. However, this Cele is somebody who could be the link between you and the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, therefore, this is an important issue. You were aware of his existence, be it only because you read the pre-trial brief. And here again, I'm not casting any reproach on you. I told you the same yesterday and you replied that you were the only accused in this Tribunal who drafted 381 applications or motions. I do take note of that. I'm not criticising you there, either. But with regard to the proceedings, I'm somewhat amazed that such an important element as this that drew your attention as you just saw, why did you wait to the very last minute to say, "I need in my language and in hard copy the statement of this man Cele." Well, you could have asked for it several months ago. All the more so, since this individual is so important to you, you could have done that months ago and you apply for this on the last day. The Prosecutor has just explained to you that he's really doing his level best. That there were many factors to take into account, for instance, that initially, you refused to accept everything on DVDs, so everything now has to be transcribed which takes time. We know that. But regardless of that, this is important. It is important to know whether Mr. Cele was under you or not. You say he didn't. And in support of your case, it would be interesting to know whether, what his position was and this position would be in the statement, but you raise this issue at the very last minute, hence my surprise. Please do understand that this is not a reproach on my part, but I'm just astonished, just as I expressed astonishment in light of the fact that the OTP should have been very aware of this CD and should have checked that you had -- Cele and you should have made sure that you had a statement in hard copy. Yes, Mr. Seselj, and then we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is my unalienable right to have all the documents submitted to me on paper and in the Serbian language. If the Prosecution is unable to do so, then this means that the international justice is impossible. It is my unalienable right to defend myself; it is guaranteed by a number of international conventions. The Prosecution has had five years at its disposal and they must have known that I would need that at one point and I have to say that I have been misled. Up until a couple of days ago, I believed that Cele was among this group of Serbian Radical Party volunteers in Zvornik. I learned later of his statement that he gave to the Prosecution and that there he says that he did not go with this group of Serbian Radical Party volunteers but that he had joined them in the organisation of the association of Serbs from Bosnia-Herzegovina to guard the Glinica Factory with a small group of people and that he had gone there from treatment at Banja Junakovic and that he remained in Zvornik until mid-May. And in late May he appeared at the Serbian Radical Party rally in Podgorica where an attempt on my life was made. He could not have been a Vojvoda at that time, he was promoted to the rank of Vojvoda only in 1993. I can agree with you that I know the most but I don't know everything, although I'm trying to learn everything but that's impossible. This is the situation that I am in. Perhaps I will obtain the statement from Miroslav Vukovic, Cele, during the break. It will be a short statement but the Prosecution has to provide the official transcript of the interview with him because we will need it for future witnesses, witnesses who had seen him there and who mention his name. So I am not denying that there is a link between me and Cele. Cele was the deputy commander of the volunteers in Trpinje in eastern Slavonia, he was promoted to the rank of the Chetnik Vojvoda. In late 1992, he was elected into the parliament on the Serbian Radical Party slate, but he was not in this group of volunteers that were sent by the Serbian Radical Party in April 1992 to Zvornik. This was all organized by the JNA. That is the gist of it. Because he remained there longer than the volunteers did. How can I prove that? On the one hand I will have the statement, on the other hand, the interview that he gave to the Prosecution. I hope that I will get the statement during the break by fax and this statement from the Prosecution should also come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have the break. If the Prosecutor during the break could find the statement in Serbian and disclose it to the accused, it would be a good thing. I don't know if 20 minutes is enough for you to find this statement. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Marcussen can answer that question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think the accused is talking about a statement that he is anticipating receiving from the witness. It's not a statement that OTP has. We have a set of recordings, not a statement. But that's correct, the accused is nodding. He's anticipating receiving a statement shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you cannot give him a hard copy in Serbian of this statement made by Mr. Cele to the OTP. You don't have this at your disposal, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I would like the registrar to tell us where we stand regarding time. If I'm not mistaken, I believe that Mr. Seselj must have an hour and 30 minutes left. Witness, please, I have a question for you and I think it's an important question, like all of my questions, but this one is really important. We have just discovered that on February 26th, 1993, i.e., not long after what happened to you, you made an official statement you signed relating what had happened, and giving the names of the perpetrators of what had been done to the prisoners. Then a few years later in 1996, you were heard by the OTP once again, and then here you integrate Seselj's men. You integrate them by drawing a sketch of the administrative building where, on the second floor, you're saying that there's presence of these -- of Seselj's men. So I'm wondering why it is that on February 26th, 1993, you didn't say it right away. Why did you wait a couple of years to say this? So I'm wondering whether your memory wasn't refreshed in 1996 and that your memory being refreshed, you were able to locate Seselj's men on the sketch. So could you please tell us what exactly this is all about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for an explanation, I gave a great many statements, different ones, to some sort of human rights organisations that were milling around me from the moment I arrived, until my latest, most recent statements. And already at the time, I knew that certain men were Seselj's men because that's what they were referred to by others while we were incarcerated and quite simply, when the investigator came in 1996, that is, I did my best to provide as detailed information as possible within the frameworks of my knowledge. Now, how come that is not to be found in what I provided in 1992 or 1993 whenever it was, 1993, I think, I can't remember having given that statement, but I'm quite sure that it was about the same people, if you look at the nicknames and everything else, you would be able to deduce that it's about the same people. Now, whether the person who took down the statement at the time skipped over certain things or -- well, I don't know. I can't really say. He might not have taken down the events as I recounted them. I can't remember now. But if you look at the chronology and look at the names of the people that appear there, then I knew in 1992 as well because the other guards and the soldiers that we came into contact with or rather we heard through the guards, that they were Seseljevci or Seselj's men, that's what people called them, so I'm telling you this on the basis of what I heard, I could not myself ascertain who belonged to what organisation, who, what, where, when. So I'm recounting it to the best of my recollections and knowledge. So neither in 1992 or 1996 can I say with certainty that they were Seselj's men and I can't do that today because I don't have insight into the documents to tell me who was a member of Seselj's party or not. I just said what I heard from the other guards and perhaps because I said that I had heard this, the person taking down the statement failed to record it, failed to put it in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for this answer. The cross-examination will now resume. The registrar gave me the time left. You have one hour and 45 minutes left, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, I assume that in the place you live now and watch television and that you follow the press, read the papers, that you have certainly heard that there was a trial ongoing in Belgrade against six persons accused of war crimes against the Muslim prisoners and civilians in Zvornik. Have you heard about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Among those six, four of them are Zoks, Toro, Lopov, and Bosonac, those were their nicknames, the names that they used. I don't even have to state their names. Do you know that they are there? And I have documents where their names appear but that's not important because it's not my intention to deal with whether they are in fact responsible and guilty of something or not. I assume that a special court for war crimes in Belgrade would have to diligently investigate this and make the right judgements, so I'm not going to doubt the outcome and I'm not going to deal with whether they did something or not. What I have here are certain documents which arrived yesterday and which I'm going to show you now and I'd like to hear your comments. They are three statements. One is a statement by Milorad Gogic, you've heard about him, have you not? He was the commander of this Loznica, group, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Anyway, he declares himself as being one of Arkan's men here and then we have Sava Sinadinovic's statement, you might not have heard of him, it's a short statement. And Vojin Vuckovic, nicknamed Zuc, I'm sure you've heard of him. I have his statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, as I have copies for all members of the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecution, that we place it on the overhead projector, the first of those documents and we'll go through it. I'm going to read out the paragraphs one by one and you can give me your comments, state your opinion and so on, what you know about whether it is true or not. First we have the statement by Milorad Gogic and we have his particular set out here, his address, the ID card number, and all other data so that the Prosecutor can check all this out during the day as he did in Goran Stopovic's case and the documents that I presented in that regard. And here is what he says, "I hereby state" and I quote, first paragraph: "That with a group of volunteers from Loznica, mostly my friends, I went to Zvornik at the beginning of April 1992 at the invitation of the late commander Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, to whom I was taken by his deputy the late Marko Pejic, Peja, who I knew from before because I was an active boxer. My group, which was in Zvornik known as Gogic's group, was the sole group that took part in the liberation of Zvornik under the commander of the Serbian volunteer guard and of course members of the guard who were not from Loznica but who were brought in there." Then he goes on to say that they never mistreated civilians or prisoners of war and that it was only after the liberation that he heard that certain crimes had been committed and that he didn't know who the perpetrators were. He assumes that they were self-organised paramilitary formations who were to blame. Then he goes on to say, "I remember that over there, the groups that were active were Pivarski's, Niski, Vojin Vuckovic, Zuca's group, the Yellow Wasps, the White Eagles, and during a certain period, a group separated from Zuca, that was led by Zena [phoen] the Chetnik and there were goodness knows how many other groups. Quite simply, a few people would gather together and without anybody's command as they saw fit, they would move around Zvornik and the surrounding parts and stories linked to looting and the persecution of civilian persons and all other acts were linked to them, acts that were not commensurate with decent soldiers of the kind that were in my group and the group I headed. Do you have any comments to make to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, during my testimony yesterday in what I said, I mentioned that we loaded up some goods for Gogic on one occasion. That's the first point. He had a red Golf car. Number two, secondly, his group, well, they called themselves as belonging to him, and they didn't come into -- but Stuka, Sarma [phoen], Kardelj, they were the people I mentioned yesterday, Mile Rogonja and the rest, friends of his from Loznica. How should I put this? They beat us most. And I do know that a prisoner, I don't want to mention his name in open session, with another man, I remember that man's name -- well, I remember him mostly by his nickname, but this group of Loznica men took them to the kindergarten, the nursery that was in the centre of Zvornik and they cleaned it up because they said the Loznicari were put up there, according to what they told me, and they said that they would come across blood everywhere and footwear and things like that when they cleaned up the place. Furthermore, a group of people who was incarcerated in the SUP building in Zvornik and there is a man, he is married now, who's still alive, and a man from Gogic's group, Stuka, the leader, carved in a cross on his forehead with a knife and you can see the scar today. So that's as far as when people said that they had nothing to do with that. Now, as for this other part, Pivarski, we would also see him, he introduced himself as Pivarski and he didn't have half a hand. And although I can't say that I ever saw him do any harm to anyone. Niski, I also mentioned him yesterday. Now, whether some things were staged or not, I don't want to go into that, but I just remember on one occasion, if I can recount a detail, if the court considers it important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Just may I have brief answers, please, because my time is limited. We will have time to go into them, you've already mentioned some things but let's see what Gogic has to say in his statement further down and then you will be able to comment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew Niski anyway. Vojin Vuckovic, Zuta, I have heard of the Yellow Wasps, or Zuta Osa. As for the Beli Orlovi White Eagles, I don't know who their leader was, there were various groups and Simo Chetnik, I don't know. I have perhaps heard of him but I really don't know about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. We -- I skipped a sentence here where he says that when he went to Zvornik, there were no members of the Serbian Radical Party there but that many introduced themselves as being Vojvodas and that is in between the two underlined paragraphs. Now he goes on to describe Zvornik's liberation on the 9th of April, he said he returned to Loznica on the 13th of April and then he was called by Colonel Stupar, he was the commander of the Special Pancevo Brigade, the unit from Pancevo, to assist in the liberation of Kula Grad. And he goes on to say that on the 26th of April, Kula Grad fell, and then on page 2, and I've underlined this portion, what I would like to focus on, which is the interesting part for you to comment, he says: "On that day, my deputy was killed, Branko Djokic. And my group together with me, that same evening withdrew from Zvornik. In the meantime, in the Zvornik MUP, as chief, Milos Pantelic was appointed, a retired policeman from Loznica, who before that was for many years chief of the traffic police. "In view of the fact that various paramilitary units which I've already spoken about continued to move around Zvornik unrestrained, I was invited by Arkan to return to Zvornik to help out Pantelic to establish law and order in town. I did go back to Zvornik at about the 10th of May, 1992 and there, I formed a special police unit and led that unit. "Since that time, I was under the command of the chief, Milos Pantelic and the chief of the state security, Goran Jugic and I received orders exclusively from them. "I was invited to come back to Zvornik, first of all because of the problems that were caused there by Zuca's unit, I immediately upon my arrival called up Zuca to have a talk with him and I gave him a deadline by which he should leave Zvornik with his men so that the situation could return to normal in town. "Zuca left Zvornik and took control of Crni Vrh. I was wounded in an action at Kamenica on the 30th of May, 1992 and the commander of the unit which I had formed was taken over by my deputy Milos Zetsic who otherwise was a staff Glinica and was born in Loznica and he was also a former boxer, very heavily-built man. "After I was wounded and after I left Zvornik while I was in hospital, I was visited by the then president of the municipality Brano Grujic and the chief of MUP, Milos Pantelic, and they complained to me that they had problems with my men, who most probably behaved in an unseemly manner because in those actions in Zvornik, we in fact had lost a number of men, specifically in Kamenica where I myself was wounded. "Of us, 23 were killed and another two in addition to me were wounded. When I recuperated, I went to Zvornik to disband the unit and I did that in mid-June 1992. "Now, whether any of my men in the meantime returned to Zvornik, I cannot know that because they were private visits and I would go there myself because at that time, I was going out with a girl from Zvornik and she is my present wife. So with my girlfriend, I went to the seaside in July and a group of people from my unit returned to Zvornik. I assume pursuant to somebody's invitation and they waited for me to return from the seaside in order to become included in the SUP of Zvornik again. I was no longer interested in anything like that and I received information that the authorities of Republika Srpska would arrest members of the paramilitary formations in Zvornik. So I definitely returned from Zvornik at the end of July, the day before this round-up and arrest. "From the very beginning, the unit that I commanded and let me repeat, it was part of the Serbian volunteer guard, and with me, there were Zeljko Mitrovic, nicknamed Stuka; Dejan, Kurkin; Novak Senadin, aka Lale who is 100 per cent invalid without an arm and a leg; Prlic, nickname Prlje; Adamovic nicknamed Sanic; Mile Curic nicknamed Rogonja; Rade Zvanji [phoen] nicknamed Kardelj; Zoran nicknamed Macak; Rajkovic, nicknamed Sarma; Roki whose name I don't remember; Zeba and others. "I do know at that time in Zvornik, there was a so-called Kraljevacka Grupa from Kraljevo which also acted independently and that the leader of that group was Dragan Slavkovic, nicknamed Toro, whom I in fact did not know but I knew of his existence. "There were some other groups there too from the territory of Zvornik municipality. In fact, they were from the surrounding villages to Zvornik, for example, Kobra, Glavonja, Jelat. A man called -- some Jovici people, I didn't know them personally because they were people from the local area and did not belong to any of the units I mentioned earlier on." Now we come to the last paragraph which says: "In Arkan's guard there was a man nicknamed Niski who after the withdrawal of the Serbian volunteer guard remained and formed his own unit which acted as a paramilitary unit. The paramilitary unit, [Indiscernible] also had a paramilitary unit. I don't know how many men it numbered. I remember that in Zvornik, there was an elderly man from Snagovo who introduced himself as being a Vojvoda and everybody addressed him as Vojvoda. He always wore a Serbian peasant cap with a cockade but he didn't belong to a single formation. I know that not a single paramilitary unit had anything to do with the Serbian Radical Party." Then he goes on to state that he gave the statement voluntarily without any pressure or coercion and that he agreed that it could be used in The Hague Tribunal. We have the stamp of the 4th Municipal Court and District Court in Belgrade on the 24th of March and it was faxed to me on the 25th of March. Now, having heard this statement of his read out or most of the statement read out, do you consider that this group, Gogic's group, represented volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please go to the bathroom very briefly and I'll be back? Very quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, can you then go over all the text during the break. I am tired from reading this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. The president, to avoid wasting time, can I please say something that is of procedural nature. I've just received by fax Miroslav Vukovic's statement and I provided it to the registry staff to photocopy that statement, I have not been provided a photocopy yet and there is also a copy from my book. It is press conference statement given in 1992 and I would like to present this to the witness as well. I delivered all this to The Hague Tribunal in 2003 together with a set of all of my 80 books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you would like to adduce part of your book which has been disclosed to the Prosecution. You asked it to be translated and it hasn't been translated. The Prosecutor, do you have any objections or not as far as this book is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think Your Honours have already allowed the use of these kind of statements and similar written material during cross-examination so in order to expedite proceedings, I'm willing to accept the use of these documents today. I would like to make a point though. The accused has read into the record an entire statement. I suspect he will be reading other material and the rest of the statements into the record. I don't know whether the accused -- what the accused's intention of doing that is but it's the Prosecution's position that this is not evidence of the truth of the contents of the statement. If the accused wants to introduce this as evidence in the case, he must do it during his Defence case and he must produce witnesses or comply with the rules of evidence for the admission of written material in court. So I just want to make sure that there's no confusion later on about whether or not the accused has introduced any evidence into the record during cross-examination. I'm sure Your Honours, of course, are not confused about this but the accused should not be under any misapprehension as to what he has managed to receive during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, as far as your book is concerned, you are not going to read all the excerpts into the transcript because this is a waste of time. Just put a question to the witness. "I have written a book which I'm sure you haven't read. On page 155, for instance, I say, this and that," and I -- you summarise it, you summarise what is on page 155 and then you put the question to him, "Do agree with me or not?" Now, if you would like to adduce this as evidence, you will have ample opportunity to adduce these documents through your own witnesses. As far as facts are concerned, the facts that were said to you by the person whom you read out, the Chamber has taken a majority decision on this, you can, on the basis of a document like this one, put a question to the witness but the Trial Chamber has decided not to admit such statements which in the view of the Trial Chamber has decided in the majority not to give it any probative value. However, you are entitled to call to witness the person who has written the statement and then you can put the question to him directly, once you call your own witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecutor launched a discussion about nothing, not for a moment did I ask for these statements to be admitted. I have obtained these statements in order to be able to present them to the witness and hear his opinion on them, his position, his experience with this regard. And in that sense, I'm using these statements. What I am denying the right of the Prosecution to do is for tendering statements directly into the file. I have the right to present the parts of different people's statements on cross-examination. I have not read the entire statement. I have read most of it and I'm just going to read short excerpts from the other statements and I believe that I marked only two passages in my book, please don't be intimidated by the number of pages, I'm not going to read the entire book but just the two marked passages, and I have photocopied the whole press conference in order to show you the entirety of that press conference and I also photocopied the title page of the book. Please, I would like to ask the Prosecution not to preempt things that are not going to happen. I have put the witness this question just to jog his memory. After having been faced with the largest part of Milorad Gogic's statement, does he still believe that the so-called group from Loznica that Gogic was in command of was a group of volunteers from the Serb Radical Party? That's all what I would like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I apologise for what happened a little while ago. And second of all, I never said that Gogic was a member of the Serb Radical Party. I put him in the Kraljevo group and here, there are a large number of names that I've also mentioned. And third of all, there are some things that are correct in the statement but there are also some things that are not correct in the statement. When we look at the names of the people who appear in the statement, you will see that in my statement, the same names appear especially people from Loznica who beat us most and who inflicted the most harm on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, I told you that four of these men are being tried in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I don't want to prejudice that matter. What I would like to hear from you is that they were not members of the Serb Radical Party although you said that you never claimed that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they were a group from Loznica with insignia of the military police. I believe that you will find it in my statements. They had the war militia's insignia, and the first time they beat us in Standards and when Niski opposed them, they said to report to Major Marko if there is something unclear to you because they had the insignia of the war police unlike Toro who had the insignia of a major, military major on the left-hand side. Those who served in the army will know that the ranks are not worn on the shoulder but on the left-hand side of the blouse. And we heard from them and from the others that their leader at the beginning was Vojvoda Cele. Why I'm saying that at the beginning because later on --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness is now talking about other things. Let's deal with Gogic's group first. Now he's talking about the Kraljevo group. And if we have agreed on Gogic's group, that they were not the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party, let's take things one at a time. Let's not allow the witness to answer my question by talking about something else. I'm asking him about one group and he's talking about another group. I just wanted to intervene in order to stop wasting time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you a short statement that deals with Pivarski because you mentioned him as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pivarski arrived on one occasion and he brought a man when we were at Ekonomija and then he came back again to inspect on us. And he told the guards not to beat that man that he had brought, I would not want to mention his name in open session. And Pivarski also came once when we were incarcerated at Ciglana and he told us that he was a fighter and that people who beat prisoners were nothing for him and he gave us cigarettes. He distributed cigarettes amongst us. He missed half a hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you do not accuse him of any crimes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I could tell he did not commit any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have a statement by Sava Sinadinovic, he is the president of the district in Banat, who says that at the time, Pivarski was not a volunteer of the Serb Radical Party and since Pivarski was killed on the 21st of January 1994, you do not ascribe any crimes to him or misdeeds to him so we don't have to deal with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and as far as I can remember, I did not see him beating anybody. I know that he did bring in some people who stayed at Ekonomija later on but I never saw him coming and torturing any of the people who were incarcerated with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you did not know at the time that he was a member of the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But he wasn't and you never claimed he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well, then. Then we don't have to deal with this statement but what we will find more interesting is a statement provided by Vojin Vuckovic, Zuca, who provides his particulars here and I don't have to repeat them. In the second paragraph of his statement, he says: "I went together with Miroslav Bogdanovic, Ulemek Semic, also known as Legija, my brother Dusa Vuckovic on the 7th of April, 1992 to Zvornik where I was arrested." Can you please put it on the ELMO. "At that moment, I did not belong to any political party although I was in possession of the membership card of the Serbian Chetnik Movement which I had left on the 3rd of September, 1991. After the liberation from detention Ulemek talked to Brano Grujic, the president of the SDS, and the unofficial commander of the TO Zvornik, Marko Pavlovic. "Upon Ulemek's proposal, the president of the SDS, Brano Grujic, appointed me the commander of the volunteers Zvornik around the 10th of April, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please read more slowly because the interpreters are having a hard time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Between the 10th and 13th of April, 1992, I was officially appointed commander of the volunteers under the command of the staff of the Territorial Defence of Zvornik. During the period that I was in Zvornik between the 9th of April and 17th of May and the 2nd of July to 22nd of July 1992, I provided the chronological description of events to the special court in Belgrade. "During my stay in Zvornik, I was familiar with the name Dragan Toro who belonged to the Kraljevo group, the group numbered about 52 members who belonged to the White Eagles. Their commander was Zoran Petrovic also known as Azedeja [phoen]. The White Eagles formation belonged to the Serbian popular renewal. The territorial staff of Zvornik had several groups of volunteers, among them was a group of volunteers from Sombor under the commands of Pivarski and I don't know his name, but we have his name, we know his name. That group numbered about 15 volunteers who were under the authority of the Territorial Defence and Marko Pavlovic. As far as I know, that group did not belong to the Serb Radical Party and they were isolated from other volunteers from the engineering barracks. The aforementioned group was not under my command either. According to my information that I received. Subsequently, the person we nicknamed Pufta is not from Serbia; he hails from Zenica in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That person did also not belong to the Serb Radical Party but to the Drina Wolves group, Captain Miloje was in command of that group and that group belonged to the Zvornik brigade. The person known as Dragan, whose family name I don't know and whose nickname was Niski, was married to a girl from Borovo Selo and he belonged to the Serbian volunteer guard whose commander was Major Pera. Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, was the Commander of Serb volunteers. Sasa, I know as a close friend, and Brano Grujic was the local. So it was possible that Brano Grujic engaged them in raising volunteers for the Territorial Defence of Zvornik. Sasa commanded the group of some 15 and 20 volunteers from Mali Zvornik but I don't know that they were members of the Serb Radical Party. Sinisa Filipovic I knew personally. He had arrived with a group of 16 volunteers from Zuma. They say that they were members of the Serb Radical Party. This group of volunteers arrived at the beginning of April and they were not deployed in any unit although they participated in the liberation of Zvornik. After that period of the 10th of April, 1992, they were assigned to the TO Zvornik and they were told to report me to the engineers together with their Commander Simo also known as Chetnik. I acted upon the order and I accepted that unit. I checked the group. I made a telephone call to the Serb Radical Party at the Ohridska Street in Belgrade in order to check on that group. The secretary whose name was Lada Zilevic [phoen] confirmed to me that the Serb Radical Party had not sent a group of volunteers from Zuma. As far as I know, Sinisa Filipovic had never served in the army because he was not more than 18 or 19 years of age at the time. I met Gogic only after the liberation of Kula after the 27th of April, 1992. In his units, there were Zeljko Stuka, Dejan, Sarma and Mila. They belonged to the boxing club in Loznica that Gogic led and they arrived in the police camouflage uniform with complete armament, long and short rifles. From Vojislav Jekic they had received weapons and they received all the orders from the Territorial Defence staff. As far as I know, this group had not been sent out by the Serb Radical Party and they did not belong to me either. Then he says about some names that he is not familiar with that they don't ring a bell, Milan Acimovic, Jaje, Sava, Brada, Brka. These names do not ring a bell and then he states that he provided his statement voluntarily, that the statement can be used and on the last page, you have a confirmation that this was certified by the 4th Municipal Court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... slowly because the court reporter can't keep up with you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in this case, I suppose that they can correct it because they have a written text before them and they can do it based on the video recording. I'm afraid that time is passing very quickly and that was the reason why I was reading quickly, but I'm going to do it more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Based on this statement, sir, do you believe that Zuca had a reason to lie when identifying these people or he can be trusted because he knew these people and he was there on the spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he lies or not, I can only say on my part, and from the facts that I'm familiar with, from what I know, I still believe that I'm not competent to say whether somebody's lying or not. There are facts which are credible. There are also facts which in my view are not credible. If I could follow you, but I would like to be able to go back to the text again, if I may, I cannot obviously say at the moment whether -- or to what extent was this group from Kraljevo close to the SRS or not but according to my information, they were close judging from what they were saying. There were other groups and names that appear in my statements as well and the two statements more or less concur, although I'd never inspected anybody's documents in order to ascertain some people's party affiliation, so I believe that there is a concurrence here because in the conversations that we listened to, they said those things. I did not have any insight into those documents. I am just basing my statement on what I saw and heard and the conclusions that I arrived at from those things. In other ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this is also an important moment. You claimed on several occasions that Dragan Toro was from Kraljevo and this man, Toro, you characterise him as a Seselj's man and you said that umpteen times. Now, we have here a statement saying that as a matter of fact, Toro is a member of the White Eagles. The White Eagles, that's another political party, that's the Serbian Renewal Movement, that's not the Serbian Radical Party. So aren't you confused in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's why I said at the outset that there are things that are accurate and things that I agree but also there are things that I don't agree with and I wanted to go back to that. So there are quite a few names that are repeated throughout my statement and that tally on what is in those statements. But based on what I saw, what I heard, what I went through, and based on what they were talking about amongst themselves, the Kraljevo group were Seselj's men. That's the way they represented themselves to us and that's how other people spoke about them. So if somebody congratulates somebody else on his promotion, that Seselj had promoted him and this other man then thanks for the congratulations then he is a member of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But why then in your statement that you provided in Vienna less than a year after your ordeal, why did you not say that these were Seselj's men, that they said that they were Seselj's men? You'd never mentioned Seselj's men. You got some more information from the Muslim secret police AID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It has been asked and answered by the witness already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj. You seem to suggest without any evidence, unless you have evidence, but if you do have evidence, you've got to produce it. You seem to say that from Vienna to The Hague, or during that period, the witness was contacted by the secret service from Bosnia-Herzegovina, that basically prompted him on this matter. What do you base this on, is this just speculation or is it something certain? If this is a certainty, you have to support this with really strong evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you saw in the case of the Croat witnesses that the Prosecution has submitted evidence to me of the fact that they had been processed by the Croatian intelligence service prior to their testimony. I know that the OTP has evidence that the AID prepped witnesses for their testimony before the Tribunal in The Hague. This is an open secret in Republika Srpska and if you are now asking me to go into the AID archives myself and to get evidence, I can't do that but the Prosecution can do that. But I have reliable information. I can't prove it. I can ask every witness whether they were questioned by the AID and every each and one of them will say no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm going to ask the question again. You know that you are under oath and if you ever do any perjury, you may find yourself in jail. You are aware of that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did the secret service contact you before you came to testify? Answer with a yes or with a no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, I can say -- fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At page 11 of your 1996 statement, second paragraph, you say that Major Dragan, nicknamed Toro, from Kraljevo had a black military booklet that a identified him as a member of Seselj's army; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may correct you, I said that on one occasion when we were loading things up in Zvornik, Major Toro took out a large sum of German marks and handed it over to Pufta telling him, "You know how to do a good job." And then from other pocket, he retrieved another heap of German marks. We were standing up there on the truck loading things up. And if you see a large amount of money, this is something that simply is quite riveting. Everybody looked at him. And there was some kind of a card that looked like a booklet. I never did say that I saw his membership card or anything. There was something left in his hand. He was holding it in his hand. It was black. I can't recall whether the letters were gold or silver but it says, Serbian Radical Party. Now, whether this was his membership card or not, I can't say that because I did not hold that in my hand. I was maybe -- the distance between the two of us was probably as the distance between me and the lady who is sitting here in front of me. I saw this large amount of cash that he was holding in his hand and this drew my attention and I looked at it and that's why I kept looking and I saw it. And that's what I said, it looked like a card.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, your statement at page 11 states something quite differently. Could I please have it up on the screen both in English and in Serbian. This can be done, this can also be shown to the public. Second paragraph, page 11 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't believe the statement is uploaded into e-court as an exhibit so we will have to work from a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please don't take the one that I have. That's the only one that I have. Could you please take it from the Prosecution. He has the Serbian version too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We are being turned into the accused's case manager, I note.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you should have been my assistants five years ago if you done your job properly because you do know that it is your obligation to prosecute those of having been suspected of committing war crimes and to provide exculpatory material to them so you were supposed to do that with the same diligence yet you failed to do so and that's the problem of the Tribunal's Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's leave aside any criticism. We'll look at this document which we're going to put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you have it in Serbian, if you don't, then I'll give it to you. I've changed my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you see it now on the ELMO? It's the second paragraph at page 11. You describe this Major Dragan, nicknamed Toro, and in last sentence, could you please read the last sentence. It is your statement. Could you please be so kind as to read the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I saw his black-coloured military ID that identified -- that said he was a member of the Seselj's army."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So what do we see from here? First of all, that this military ID was black; is that right? And you had to see it from closer up to be able to read that he was a member of Seselj's army. Did it say Seselj's army on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was. I probably said, I can't recall word for word what I said, but I said what I told you. And probably as it was interpreted into English and then back into Bosnian, some things were worded differently and this is probably why this sentence reads as it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, did you read the statement before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please read out slowly that sentence in your language, because we have the English version which is being challenged. And it starts with the following word in your language, "video," so please read out that sentence slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I saw his black military ID where it was written he was a member of Seselj's army."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I asked for the Serbian and the English version to be put side by side, if it's possible. It was possible before when the Prosecution calls its evidence, then it's possible. You don't have the English. What's the problem? You can put one underneath the other. You can maybe bend the sheet of paper and put it right underneath it. I'm all for modern technology, I'm an expert. I would have found a solution right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar tells me that that can be done on e-court, to have a split screen. And we can see that on the ELMO as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... coloured military ID that identified him as a member of the Seselj army." [Interpretation] It's a perfect translation, even I, who can't speak English, can tell you that let alone those who actually speak English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the booklet was black and it identified him as a member of Seselj's army. Well, I can't speak English but it's all crystal clear to me right away. So it's the same, sir, in both statements both in the English version and in the Serbian version, is that not so, Mr. VS-1013?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not an expert for English language but that's probably what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So in order for you to state that, you first had to see the black military ID card; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me go back to what I've already told you and that is the way in which I saw it, the circumstances. I explained to you how I came to see it. I'm sure that after reading this statement, when most -- when 90 per cent of the things are correct, you don't go back to every comma, every --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we understood what you said, but you saw a card, a black card from a distance saying "Serbian Radical Party," why don't you conclude from that that this is a card for a political party? Whilst what you say that this is a card whose holder is a member of the army. So you're talking about two different things. What you saw, which was in black, Serbian Radical Party or something like that, why do you draw the conclusion that this shows that that person belongs to Seselj's army, if he had an army at all. As far as you know, did Mr. Seselj have an army?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some objections to your question, Mr. President. The witness never mentioned the Serbian Radical Party nor are there any black ID cards of the Serbian Radical Party. He said a military ID card where it was written that he was a member of the -- of Seselj's army. And throughout his statements, he talks about Seselj's army and for me this is the crucial part of his statement because this is where his whole testimony fails and that's why I am insisting on this. I'm not going to insist on anything else. First of all, what are those military ID cards that are black? Nobody has ever seen them. I think that thousands of witnesses have gone through the OTP and nobody ever mentioned any black military ID cards on any side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, this piece of cardboard or this card that you saw from a distance of some 10 metres because you said that you were some distance which is the distance between the lady in front of me and you, so that is some 10 metres. What enables you to say that this card you saw was a military ID card? My question is this: Aren't you making some confusion with a card showing that that person who holds it is a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot remember what I had said at that time exactly, word for word, but I always say I heard, I thought, whenever I'm talking about things that I did not personally see. When I was giving this statement, I probably said to the person taking the statement that it was probably this ID card. I did not see this ID card to be able to claim that with 100 per cent certainty. So I probably said it was probably some kind of a membership ID card or a military ID card just as I said that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could that have been an ID card from a funeral society? You know that those things exist. You pay a certain fee on an annual basis and then they pay for your funeral when you die. How were you able to say that this was a military ID card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know that it was a military ID card. I didn't see it. I assumed that this was some kind of a military ID card or a membership ID card. Secondly, it could have been of any character because I didn't hold it in my hands. I wasn't able to see whether it contains the information about the military assignment but let me repeat that I probably phrased this in the same way as I did just now because I always indicate that there is a certain level of probability involved in what I say if this is something that I did not see myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I am asking you about things that you say you saw. You did your national service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I assume that you remember what the military ID card or booklet of the JNA looked like. It was olive-green, it contained about 40 or 50 pages, it was maybe 12 by 6 centimetres, well, approximately something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, this booklet, was it the same size, bigger or smaller, thicker or thinner, than the military JNA booklet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was smaller and thinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say smaller and thinner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it was black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was black and there was a cockade on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean the two-headed eagle, the Serbian coat of arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, did it say on it, "Seselj's army"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did it say the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So on that booklet, it was written the Serbian Radical Party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it says Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well then it could have been a membership card of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well it could have been. It was some sort of card and in format and size, it was in between the old type of ID cards used in the former Yugoslavia and a military booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the Serbian Radical Party now has about half a million members and this is broadcast over the internet, it will be shown on Serbian television this evening. And all half million people and those 10.000 who used to be members and then left the Serbian Radical Party know full well that the Serbian Radical Party never had black booklets or the Serbian Chetnik movement either, absolutely never. So are you sure that that was a membership card then of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. The witness didn't say that he knows that it was a membership card of the Serbian Radical Party, it was put to him as a proposition that it could have been a membership card. He said, yes, it could have been and now he is being confronted with this as if he affirmed himself that it actually was a membership card.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another angle that nobody ever saw before me. You saw this card with bank notes, we agree on that, don't we, this card was held together with bank notes. The bank notes must have been taken from Muslims because it seems that they were looting at the time. Couldn't this card have come from somebody else? What is there that makes it possible for you to connect the one holding the card and him? Couldn't that card have been found somewhere else or couldn't he have held the card? Because if it was his own card it would be in his own wallet. These bank notes, from what I understood, did not seem to come from the wallet of that individual.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Judge, he didn't take it out of his wallet, he took it out together with the money, the wad of money that I think he took out of this pocket here and then he separated that from the wad and held it in his hand. And I said this -- well, it appears that I claim but I said that I drew the conclusion on the basis of what I saw it said on it and with the double-headed eagle, that that was it. Because while he was handing over the money, he was holding this in his other hand and then put it back in his right hand and then put it back in his left hand pocket. So I can't say with 100 per cent certainty that it was his, that's my first point because I didn't see what it actually said inside, I just assumed, this is my assumption. I assumed that it belonged to him and that that was it, but I can't say with 100 per cent certainty that it might not have been his proposal for a new card, for a new party card or whatever, but I just saw this in his hand and from that I deduced what I did and said that I assumed that that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, maybe we should move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. Do you remember seeing the words, "Serbian Radical Party" written on it as you said on page 70, line 11?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Serbian Radical Party in the transcript, Serbian Radical party. I don't know whether what you said was translated properly. This is why I put the question to you again. Did you see the written words "Serbian Radical Party"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it said, the Serbian Radical Party with the two-headed eagle. Now, how that was formulated, well, sometimes I speak fast, so I go on from one thing to another. Now, how it was recorded ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Since you mention in your prior statement "Seselj's army," you do not speak of the Serbian Radical Party in your prior statement, did you draw a conclusion from the fact that the words Serbian Radical Party were written, did you deduce from that, deduct from that or deduce that it was Seselj's army? You see there is a contradiction and I don't quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that was my conclusion. That was my conclusion. Now, legally speaking, I don't know how you differentiate between the two. At home, we -- well, there are a lot of surnames that come from somebody's name, so the followers of someone usually take their name from the leader, that's why I might have said it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Remember that you are a fact witness so you're not here to draw conclusions, you are to testify as to the facts. Please remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, in your statement, the statement which you signed, you said: "I saw his black-coloured military ID on which it said that he was a member of Seselj's army." Now, the fact that you're trying to make this statement relative now is another matter altogether. However, on that same page you go on to say the following when referring to Zoks and Pufta and Sasa, that they held certain ranks in Seselj's army. First of all, let me ask you how you recognised these men as being Seselj's army, did it say Seselj's army on the uniform, perhaps? What did it say on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I identified them the way other people, the militaries and paramilitaries called them and they referred to them as Seseljevci or Seselj's men. So I just took on this -- over this title and that's what I called them later too.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not going to tire you anymore with this because I've achieved my purpose because your entire statement and testimony has fallen through on that one point. I'd like to draw your attention to the documents that I received from the Prosecutor, some of them I found myself. You've already said that you had heard that the special court in Belgrade is conducting a trial against six individuals and I'd like to refer to the transcript now of those legal proceedings from the interview of Dragan Slavkovic, nicknamed Toro of the 1st of December, 2005, where on page 5 he explains the following: He says that as a reservist, he was engaged by Major Ratko Radojevic and Vesko Cvetkovic from Kos. And on page 16 it says that as a sniper from the 12th to the 15th of April, he carried out a certain assignment and went back home to Kraljevo. Do you think he's telling the truth there or do you still claim that he was a member of what you called Seselj's army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I saw him at Standard and with a group, Zoks and Pufta and later some others, he took us over towards the end of May and the beginning of June. Now what he did from the 4th to the 12th of April or May, I really don't know. What I do know is that he came to Standard when we were in Standard, that he filmed us with a video camera, we had to give our first and last names, tell him where we were from and so on, and afterwards, I saw him at the Ekonomija when he beat Bubica. I don't think this. I claim this, I state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to reply what we already heard during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim, I can't remember the date but whether it was the end of May or beginning of June, I'm not quite sure, up until the beginning of July or the end of June, we went with him and loaded up certain goods in Zvornik. And the group that he led at the time, other people referred to that group as Seseljevci, Seselj's men and that's all I can tell you. The other soldiers and other groups referred to them as Seselj's men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you didn't remember that when you gave your statement in Vienna, isn't that right? And now I come to my next question: In the transcript from the examination -- or from the 2nd of December, 2005 on page 30 in the trial in Belgrade, the accused Ivan Korac, nicknamed Zoks, states that as a volunteer he arrived in Zvornik at the invitation of the Serbian association from Bosnia-Herzegovina with its headquarters in Belgrade, Terazije 5 is the address, and he joined Stojan Pivarski's unit where there was Darko Jankovic, Pufta, and Savo, who's surname he doesn't know. Do you think he's lying in that statement in the trial against him, that he has reason to lie about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you is this: As far as I know, and it's up to the Court to determine who is lying and who is not and I think I've been invited here as a witness to see what he saw, where he saw it, and how it happened, I know that Zoks went to Standard, used to come to Standard. I know that he went to the Ekonomija with Vojvoda Cele and that he beat the father of one of the prisoners whose father succumbed to the injuries and died.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But I'm asking you something else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. I want to tell you what I know about Zoks. He can say he's Prince Charles, as far as I'm concerned. I'm not an attorney but I'm going to tell you what I know about him and I want to say that I was a witness when Zoks, and I didn't say this because I didn't have time to do that, he targeted Kemal Korkutevic with something, with a cord and he was so frightened that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the Trial Chamber should intervene here. Judges, I can't challenge the story told by this witness about what happened to him. Probably a large portion of his testimony is the truth, I don't challenge that because crimes did happen. I assume he was beaten up. But from the statement that he gave in Vienna, we can see that that was of lesser intensity than later on. And here, the Prosecutor asked for gymnastics in the courtroom, putting up one hand and putting down another instead of giving us a medical report telling us that he couldn't use his left arm properly. But I don't challenge the fact that he went through a lot of suffering and there's no need for him to repeat his testimony and waste my time. I don't want to interrupt him and intervene. I think that that's what the Trial Chamber should do and ask him to focus on answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, the only question we're interested in as Judges is the following: We need to know whether the group, Toro, Pufta, Zoks, Sasa, and Sava were volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. You seem to say that they were. However, you are saying this because your other comrades were saying so. So this is the core of the matter. We have a number of elements that seem to contradict this. For example, Zoks's statements and the statements of the others of Toro and so on. They seem to be people hailing from Kraljevo. So are you 100 per cent sure that people were saying that these were Seselj's men or are you less than 100 per cent sure of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, according to everything I learned while I spent time down there, not under the influence of my friends who were together there with me, and if I want to meet them today, I would hope that we discuss much nicer things because I can't put anything right, what happened happened and I have to live with that so I try to avoid those topics when I see them and talk to them today. So I avoid the subject, that's my first point. My next point is this, on several occasions I drew my own conclusions and I have been accused of lying so I want to tell you what I saw and heard. The other groups of the Serbian military and paramilitary formations referred to them as Seselj's men. So it wasn't from my friends, it was from these other units and formations who called them that way. I took that on board and that's how I referred to them. I didn't see IDs for me to be able to say that they were certainly that. And a moment ago, the conclusions that I made on the basis of what I experienced and my suffering are quite simply it turned out that I didn't have the right to make any conclusions so I'm just saying what I saw and what I heard now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, resume.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, that is in collision with your Vienna statement. When you gave the statement in Vienna, you hadn't heard that but you seem to have heard it several years later when this was needed for certain political purposes; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you tell me what political purposes you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the political purposes thought up by the secret Muslim service, AID.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you accusing me of something, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I am accusing you of instrumentalising your suffering. You were a victim, you are a victim. May I just say this to the witness, I'm not insulting him in any way by saying it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is the third time the issue come up about the allegation that there has been somebody influencing the witness. Your Honours already ruled on this, that it was inappropriate without any substantiation and now it's going on again, so I object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj. You alleged this. I asked this of the witness directly. He denied it so don't come back, please. You're wasting your time and you're wasting everybody's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj. Mr. Seselj, you have referred a few times to the declaration of the -- or the statement made in Vienna. Could you please refresh my memory. To whom was this statement given?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This statement was given to the representatives of the Muslim authorities in Sarajevo, the name of the person is mentioned at the end. It was a lady. Let's avoid going into closed session, I don't want to repeat the name, but you saw it and I can find it for you again if need be. So the Muslim authorities from Sarajevo sent people to talk to the immigrants and take statements about the sufferings that they went through before they fled abroad. I'm not doubting the veracity of that statement. I am doubting the subsequent build-up and what the witness asked me just a minute ago. I really do believe that he is a victim, that he went through a huge ordeal. I'm not contesting that. I know that there were crimes in Zvornik. However, this suffering of his is being instrumentalised by a build-up that happened later. The Serbian Radical Party is now being artificially imposed upon this witness and I would like to say that I have completely contested and challenged this statement which is based on the identification and of the military ID of Seselj's army. But then his basic story about his sufferings and ordeal, I believe it's true and I don't think anybody would be able to make all that up but I also believe that these sufferings were built upon subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's time for a break. We will break for 20 minutes and we will resume at 10 after 12. You will have 45 minutes left. So theoretically we should be able to finish the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing can resume. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1013, now we are going to deal with the statement provided by Miroslav Vukovic, Celo, which I received only recently.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been copied for the Judges and the Prosecutor. And I would also kindly ask for it to be placed on the ELMO. We're going to go through just three short passages in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, he provides his particulars where he was born, where he resides, the number of ID, and so on and so forth. The Prosecutor has already interviewed him for hours. He says: "I state that I went to Zvornik on the 17th of April, 1992; that I was not the leader of Seselj's men from Kraljevo, neither that I went to Zvornik through the SRS. The Serbian Radical Party did not have a unit from Kraljevo in the territory of Zvornik. On several occasions I returned to Serbia and then went back to Zvornik in order to provide the humanitarian aid. I left Zvornik for good on the 17th of May, 1992, when the JNA withdrew from Zvornik." You see here that he denies your allegations that he was in command of the Kraljevo group. But what is interesting -- even more interesting is the next paragraph in which he says that you provided a false description of him. He watched the recording of the trial yesterday on TV and he says: "Yesterday, I watched the trial of Dr. Vojislav Seselj at the Hague Tribunal and I was surprised with the lies that were provided by the protected witness. I do not resemble physically to the man that he describes as Vojvoda Celo, and in the period that the witness talked about, I was not in Zvornik. My height is between 172 and 175 centimetres. At that time I did not weigh 100 kilos. I didn't have a big belly; I don't have it now either. I don't have dark eyes. I never sported long black hair. I did not have a long beard. I never died either my beard or my hair. I never had colours in my hair. I'm a normal man." So he denies the description that you provided to this Court. What do you say? Is he telling the truth? Or maybe you were confused when you were providing your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, I'm not a painter, I can't paint him. I tried to describe him based on my memory, the way I remember him. Whether we are talking about the same height or the same weight, after such a long period of time, that's how I remember him. You know that it is very difficult to pinpoint somebody's weight or height just by looking at them. I believe that my memory was much better then than it is today, but I believe that I described him to the best of my recollection and knowledge. Maybe I was off by a few centimetres or a few kilogrammes. Yesterday, when I was describing him, I said that I did my best to try and estimate their height and weight, if that person was standing next to me. After a certain period of time, it's very difficult to recollect everything. I provided the description to the best of my recollection and knowledge. As for the rest that was said, the person that we saw in Standard was referred to as Vojvoda Celo. The person that we saw at Ekonomija was also referred to as Vojvoda Celo, which means that I adhered to my statement that he appeared at Standard. And I also want to say that I adhere to what I said, that he appeared at Ekonomija. How, who called him, how he arrived, I don't know. I did not have an insight into that, and this goes beyond my competencies. I am here to say what I saw and what I know and what I assume is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, since you have identified so well, how come it never struck you that he limps? You know what it means when a person limps. You come from Bosnia; you understand the word. How come you didn't notice that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were at Standard, Sasa told us that this gentleman should not be looked in the eyes and we had to lower our eyes. I don't know whether he limped or not. I don't remember that. And you know that any normal person who is afraid sees things differently and cannot remember all the details. I described him to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He denies the description that you provided and believes that you have confused him with somebody else, and he goes on to say this: "After the 14th of September, 1991, I have been an invalid of war." And I would like to add to that that he was wounded in eastern Slavonia. And the witness must have noticed that and I would like to add that everybody notices that about him, that he limps. He goes on to say that he says that a bayonet that you normally mount on an automatic rifle, it's a very short metal knife. You know how the bayonet on the Kalashnikov looks like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well, then. He says: "I had a bayonet on an automatic rifle and I wore it by my left knee, tied by two ropes; one below the knee and the other above the knee?" You know that our soldiers copied heros from American movies and wore their bayonets tied around their legs, and that's how he describes himself. I would like to call upon Mr. Ulrich Mussemeyer, who interviewed me for three days at the Office of the International Criminal Tribunal in Jelena Grusic Street in Belgrade, who saw me and I call upon him to confirm this. He signed this and this was certified by the second municipal court in Belgrade. You could not identify Zuca either, and at the end of your statement you said that there were two men by the name Zuca. Do you remember that? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you say in the last paragraph -- actually, the penultimate paragraph, that there was one Zuca who was a military officer from Belgrade and that he appeared while you were looting houses in the centre of Zvornik in a car Sierra with Swiss registration plates; that he was very tall, and Toro told that you this was Zuca from Zemun. And in the last paragraph, you say there was another Zuca, Vojin Vuckovic, brother of Dusan Repic, and so on so forth. You go on talking about him but that is not important. Are you aware that you are the only person who mentions two men by the same nickname Zuca, that nobody else noticed that, that nobody else is aware of an JNA officer by the name of Zuca, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, the person whom Major Toro identified as Zuca from Zemun, that man pulled over in a blue Sierra with Swiss registration plates. He got out of the car.
