He was sturdily built. And Toro greeted him. He told him, "Good day, brother." And Toro treated him with respect. This is what I can tell you. When that man left, then Toro said, "This is Zuca. He is from Zemun. He is a military special. He either is or will be the new chief of defence of the town, and he is a good fighter." This second Zuca -- the first Zuca and the second Zuca I saw only once. The descriptions that I provided about this first Zuca with whom Toro exchanged greetings, I believe that he had a butterfly tattoo on his neck. As far as I could see and as far as I could describe, the persons that I saw at the moment, I did it to the best of my recollection and knowledge. I tried to provide the best possible description of that person. I'm sure that I saw this Zuca in the centre of Zvornik. He pulled the car over next to the kindergarten. In the centre of Zvornik there is a street between the Namaca building and kindergarten. He pulled the car over there. And we were loading furniture in Zvornik. And the second Zuca that I was talking about is the person that I saw when -- in Zamlac. This is a part of Zvornik where we were loading furniture onto the lorries. He came and he was just watching us. Zoks was with us at the time. He told them that we were good, that everything was okay with us. And then this person told us that this Zuca is a crazy man, he is a lunatic. I don't know whether he said he is crazy or he is just a little crazy. I don't remember that. But this is my only recollection about that meetings with these two people. People who interviewed me insisted on me trying to describe these people to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that towards the end of July 1992, the authorities of Republika Srpska arrested paramilitary formations from the territory of Zvornik; that a lot of people were arrested on that occasion and that the group included Zuca's group as well? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I have a problem. Before we move on to another statement or something of that kind, I would like to get back to the previous statement made by Vukovic, aka Cele, because I need to look at the last page and put a question to the witness. The reliability and probative value of this is important. I need to understand what the source of this document is because I find there's some confusion here. On the last page, on page 9 I believe, if I'm not mistaken, there is an official stamp together with a signature. I would like to reconstruct this. Is the witness able to read this? And then we can have the translation of what we have on our screen. Can you tell us what this stamp means? What is inside the stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number is 5007. I think that then it goes on to say 2000, the number is not very legible. Then it says Miroslav Vukovic signed in his own hand this document or confirmed that the signature on this page -- I think, I can't really read it as his, the identity is confirmed on the basis of ID card number 195376. And the identity is -- has been confirmed on the basis of personal ID cards number then it's -- there's nothing there. The appropriate tax has been paid and then it says here, the second instance, court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 26th of March, 2008. So this is a certified signature of the person who has made the statement. We don't know who was present when this statement was made. Is that how you understand things and is that in line with what's being translated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way I see it, this means that he gave a statement and the credibility of his statement is guaranteed by his personal ID card.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please listen. Let's get back to the truthfulness of this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, Judge Lattanzi said March 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that we are discussing the truthfulness or the validity of the ID card and not of the statement, have I understood this correctly or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, well, I'm not a lawyer but the way I see it as much as I can understand these things, this means that his identity was confirmed on the basis of his ID card and that this is his signature and that he stands behind all that he wrote there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, good. That's what I understood. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If I may make a comment, Your Honours. I just like to reiterate the observation that I made before that at this stage, this document cannot be introduced into evidence and in my respectful submission, there cannot be an issue of the veracity of the contents of this declaration. It's something that has -- certain facts have been put by Mr. Seselj to the witness. It's being proposed that the witness is wrong based on another description of -- by this person. The statement cannot be admitted into evidence at this stage. Either the witness have to come or the statement would have to go in under 92 bis or 92 ter if those requirements can be made at this stage -- at a later stage, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, Mr. Seselj has not asked this to be tendered into evidence. Nonetheless, in order to have a source of reference, because we did, in the end, read out the statement, it's on the record, and that's why it is important to understand where this comes from. It's not only a question of tendering it into evidence or not of admitting it or not, it has to do with the way in which we will weigh this because it's on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed to say something here. The competent judicial organ does not confirm the veracity of the statement but the authenticity of the signature and that's the only thing that matters to us. As to the contents of the statement, we will be discussing this throughout this trial and I am opposed to the Prosecution tendering the -- any statement into evidence just like that, I am opposed to the Defence doing the same thing. The trial must be public but this statement confirmed as authentic by a judicial organ is slightly better than what the Prosecution has offered at times, but I'm not asking for it to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could you please put the front page of the book "Milan Panic Must Fall." I marked three passages in this book. This is the book that I provided to the Prosecution in late 2007 in the batch of 80 books. It contains all my press conferences from 1992 and the one that is -- I'm drawing your attention to is from the 6th of August, 1992. It begins at page 150 and goes on to 152. I'll read just the parts that were marked. "At this press conference when the news came in that the authorities of the Republic of Serbia arrested some volunteers in the municipality of Zemun, I say the following: The Serbian Radical Party welcomes the action of the authorities of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to disarm various, as we call them, paramilitary formations which are nothing but bands of thugs that were terrorising the peaceful civilian population regardless of their ethnicity and religion. Breaking up various smuggling channels, war profiteering and so on, we believed that it was high time for such a move to be made and that those gangs of thugs should be disarmed, brought to justice, and be held responsible for all those things that they did in the several months in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which inflicted a great deal of political, economic and moral damage, primarily to the Serbian people. "Incidentally, those gangs of thugs did not make any contribution to the war effort in any serious combat. They did not take part in any serious combat. All they did was based on looting and terrorising of civilians. The Serbian Radical Party had nothing to do with them. Some of them were our volunteers in northern Slavonia, it should actually read eastern Slavonia, so there is a mistake here, and we forced them out of our ranks because of their looting, thefts, and inappropriate behaviour and lack of discipline. But most of them have had no contacts, nothing to do with us at all. "We believe that in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there can exist only one military organisation and that is the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and nothing else." Sir, Witness VS-1013, is this a clear example of distancing from those paramilitary gangs from the area of Zvornik in your opinion? What is your opinion? Had you heard this on TV, what would you have said at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me give you my opinion on what you've just read. I think first of all, that it is too late, because if it's August 1992, as you said, at that time, Zvornik and most of the towns along the River Drina had already been ethnically cleansed. I know that for a fact for Zvornik, I don't know exactly for other places. I welcome any action, any initiative aimed at preventing violence against other human beings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that this was the 6th of August, 1992, before the Tribunal in The Hague was established. As far as I can remember, the ICTY was established in 1993, so this is not an expression of fear or an attempt to shift the blame. It is simply a political response to an event, and I think that you will agree that the Serbian Radical Party at that time was not the ruling party and it could not, on its own, do as it pleased in those matters through its authorities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know much about politics. As far as I know, you were not in power at the time, that is true, and as far as the text is concerned, if this was the view of the Serbian Radical Party, then I can say that this is perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now let me go to page 155, if you would be so kind as to show it on the ELMO. When asked by a journalist I give a lengthy response. It's about the events in Pijelje [phoen] so let me just read the part that pertains to Bosnia-Herzegovina. "In Bosnia-Herzegovina, we don't have any military organisations of our own, no formations, but there are our members who are fighting there in the ranks of the Serbian army. After all, we have a highly-developed Serbian Radical Party in the Serbian Chetnik movement in Bosnia-Herzegovina and all our members there are at the forefront of the struggle for the freedom of their people and the salvation of their territories and according to all testimonials, they are amongst the most conscientious, most disciplined and the bravest. "The issue of discipline in the ranks and their compliance with the commands of the Serbian army is never in question. If anyone does anything in -- on our behalf that is subject to sanctions, we always do all we can to bring this person to justice, to have them criminally prosecuted for what they did and no orders were ever given by the Serbian Radical Party for such acts. So all those war profiteers, smugglers and looters are a normal occurrence in every war. "Throughout our involvement in the struggle of the Serbian people of Serbian Krajina, we have always fought about that. You have seen yesterday at the press conference some guy by the name of Vukan Drepin [phoen], who was threatening with liquidation and he had some execution list, he was forced out of the ranks of the Serbian Chetnik Movement in September 1990. He appeared as a volunteer in Slavonia in Borovo Selo, he spent a couple of days, he stole four grenades and fled. "Later on, he joined Arkan, somewhere around Tenja and then he stole nine uniforms and I don't know how many weapons and when he was found out, he fled again. "So we are talking about people like that. And now they are making those execution lists and let me just add, those execution lists were made in Belgrade, some organisation named the Black Hand was set up and my name was on this execution list. So now they are making those execution lists but the problem is that they are simply registered as parties, some kind of royalist blocks, and they can simply convene the press conference. Journalists cannot verify what is behind what they are saying and what isn't. The public treats them as a serious political party and that is why we need to reregister so that we know what is a party and what is not, lest all kinds of psychos and criminals could hog the limelight in the manner that is properly used by political parties and not to criminal gangs. Some man by the name of Zuca was in Zvornik. He had the biggest gang, criminal gang there. He was our volunteer up until the last fall in Slavonia, and he was forced out because of lack of discipline, because of looting. But he managed to go to Zvornik with his gang and he caused mayhem there and this is why they had to do that. Did you in Bosnia-Herzegovina have a situation where the multi-party system was brought back, where at first, there was a huge number of political parties that were registered because the criteria were low?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For instance, in Serbia, it was enough for somebody to gather 100 signatures and to register a political party. I think it was something similar in your country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never tried to set up a political party but I believe this is why it was what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that that's why I urge for the more stringent criteria for the registration of parties. And now I have a question of the journalist. Don't you think that at this time, you will be the only one to try and punish the criminals? This journalist had in mind our previous efforts to stamp out war profiteering, smuggling and crime. At page 156, I give the following answer: "I consider that the Serbs should arrest somebody if they pilfer during the war and if somebody killed civilians and if somebody abused civilians. We Serbs always had an army of knights that --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I'm sorry. Perhaps the Judges disagree with me, but I don't think this is right. You are testifying. You are reading out entire pages. That is my personal point of view and you are making fun of us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, these aren't pages and pages, they are just three excerpts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, rather than reading out pages and pages, and smart people would say that you are advertising your book, it might have been better to put the question to the witness in such a way, "In a book I wrote, I criticised the criminals and asked the paramilitaries to be dismantled. Have you heard of anything of that sort?" The witness then can answer, "I have heard about it. I haven't heard it. I don't know anything about your book." Then you move on to something else. Because, in fact, this technique is designed to make us understand that you took a public stance against the paramilitaries, against those people who were acting under various political labels whereas these were mere criminals. This is understandable. You can call your own witnesses and you can adduce your own evidence, but in this case, we have a witness who is not a Serb, he certainly hasn't read your book, and he can't help you much with his answers. So this is what we are telling you and we are telling you this in your own interests. It's not to prevent you from defending yourself. This is in our own interest. All this time we have spent on this could have been cut down to a few sentences and you could have put your questions. I'll give you the floor back.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, this book is an authentic document dating back to 1992. It's a document for which I consider that the -- I'm sure the Prosecution doesn't mean to challenge it. Secondly, from this entire book I'm just reading out three paragraphs, and I started reading the third one a moment ago, and it is on that basis that I wanted to ask the witness a number of questions and round off my cross-examination. Now, this seems to bother you. I think that the book is sufficient proof and compulsive evidence. Now, the witness hasn't read the book and you haven't read the book and it seems that the Prosecution hasn't read the book either so these three paragraphs must have been read and if you read the whole book you'll come across many similar examples whereas as it so happens this relates to the arrest of paramilitary gangs in Zvornik and you weren't even ready to wait for me to ask my question. May I be allowed to continue and then ask my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just put your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to read the third paragraph before I do that because without it there is no question. I can't ask my question. Just three minutes of your patience. I don't think that's too long. I do expect those three minutes of patience on your part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have 15 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I consider that the Serbs should arrest someone if they pilfer during the war, if somebody killed civilians, if somebody abused civilians. We Serbs always had a chivalrous army which fought the enemy as you would fight an enemy on a battlefield but it never used to test its bravery over women, children or civilians of any nationality. And I consider that the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina did well for starting to instill law and order on its territory and these gangs of thugs tried to take over power in Zvornik after all. That happened too and nobody could deal with them. Sometimes, you find yourself in a situation very easily as in a situation like that. It hasn't happened yet but it might happen that these gangs of thugs, some will violate a truce if a truce is established and stage a conflict. If you cannot keep a military formation under control on your own territory, then quite simply, you've lost. You've lost the battle. Discipline must be respected and the authority of power must be respected as well. You know, if Serbian authority has been established, then all the formations must listen to that Serb authority and be accountable to it, to carry out its instructions. If somebody fails to do that then he represents an impediment, an obstacle to that Serb authority. And especially in cases where they didn't loot Muslims and Croats but principally the Serbs who happened to be on their territory, in order to loot Croats and Muslims, they would have to cross over to their territory in principle, they're all great cowards and they're not inclined to do that, and then they take what they find closest to hand. That's where they act and they carried over some property over here. Now, Mr. VS-1013, are you familiar with a situation like that, that in Zvornik, there was looting of Muslim property first and when there was no more Muslim property to loot, they started looting Serb property? I think you said something about that too yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that situation and I said that during yesterday's testimony, what happened was people would light up Serb house on a house, they would knock on the door, Toro did that, and when nobody came to open the door, then he would say, "Break in." He would tell us to break in. We would storm the house and he would pick some items that he took a fancy to and we had to load them up on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that in the spring of 1992, large groups of Serb refugees from Tuzla appeared, Zivinice and even from Kladanj as well, Srebrenik and other places in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am aware of that because while we were loading up goods all over Zvornik, people would come in frequently and select houses and then they tried to send us away and say that that was going to be their property from now on because they had taken it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But they had left their property behind, what they had in Tuzla, Kladanj and other places; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they now sought refuge and they looked for abandoned Muslim houses to move into and they wanted to have the furniture remain this in those houses whereas these gangs of thugs did not allow that but seized furniture and anything else, any other goods they found in them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they didn't demonstrate elementary humaneness. If people were left without a roof over their heads and left behind all their property, they come to Zvornik and see property abandoned by the Muslims and they didn't even have the possibility of moving into these abandoned houses because these gangs of thugs, first of all, wanted to loot the properties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd just like to put you right because most of the Muslims were expelled and what remained, all of them were gathered together in front of the department store and they were sent to Subotica, women and children, and they were forbidden to take any property with them except what they could fit into small bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, we'll have a possibility of testing and seeing whether the Muslims were expelled, how they came to leave, whether there was pressure or not. I don't say that they didn't leave. I do agree that there was pressure to make them leave but no official persecution but they were mistreated which made them reach a decision to leave, like your arrest, like the fact that people were beaten, looted property and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was able to learn from what people told me and from what I saw, the people who stayed on in Zvornik the longest, remained behind the longest sometime in mid-July were collected together in front of the department store, they told me that, I didn't see that with my own eyes so I can't say that this is 100 per cent correct, I'm just telling you what I heard so don't take me to task there. They told me they had been gathered together in front of the department store, made to get on to buses, and then they were driven off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Some of them said they said they wanted to be taken to Serbia and then from then on to foreign countries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to deny that. Maybe some people did request that. I know that the group who told me about it, I don't know how many of them there were in the group, they said they had been rallied up in front of the department store, boarded into buses and then driven off. Now, whether they bequested their property to the Serb municipalities, I'm not challenging what you're saying but that's what this last group of people told me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and make pauses between question and answer, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, slow down, please, and make a pause between question and answer and the same goes for the witness. Thank you very much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since I have only a few minutes left, I am trying to squeeze in at least two more questions and obtain answers for these questions, but I'll slow down. Were there cases, according to your knowledge, that Serbs who had already left Tuzla, Kalesija, Zivinice, Kladanj and other places, not to mention all of them, that had already been harmed, harassed or beaten, that there had been killings there as well and so on and so forth, were there cases that these Serbs behaved revengefully towards the Muslim population that they found in Zvornik when they arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information and according to what I learned from other people, I did not see these things. I wasn't there but I only heard about them, there were cases of people having lost somebody, but this was on a much lesser scale than the crimes that were committed by what you yourself called gangs of thugs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But they were the cases that I described as well, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not to such a large scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The gangs were the biggest problem for everybody in Zvornik but they were the biggest problem for Muslims, would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may take up a bit more of your time, I would like to say that we are all responsible for the situation that we are in charge of. Those people who had taken over the power were responsible for peace and order. There is no war without victims. We are all aware of that. But there is one more thing here. If I tried to do something to the best of my abilities and then I do nothing but harm to all of those around me, then I am responsible. That's what power and authorities are for. You knew most of these people as you say from Croatia and they had done the same thing so it's impossible that these things could not have been prevented and it is impossible that these people who brought these people in were not aware of whom they were bringing in. I am not saying that you could be responsible for all of them, and that you could control all of them but I am comparing this to a state. A state is responsible for peace and order in the state and along the same lines, the municipal power in Zvornik was supposed to keep peace and order in Zvornik which they didn't do. They did not honour what they were supposed to do. The gangs had been invited and did whatever they wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, the situation was chaotic. I stated that in other places, the Prosecutor showed it on some video clips but I won't go through that at the moment. I'm going to show you another typical example of a group retaliation, you mentioned the killing of (redacted) didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was killed when you were detained or -- before your eyes almost?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you also hear a story about him having been killed by some locals because he had been an Ustasha. In 1945, he came with his Ustasha unit to the property in Trsic village and on that occasion, Vojo Camic and Nikola Zekic were killed. After the war, this (redacted) was not brought to justice. According to my information, some people recognised him, people from Zvornik and the environs, they remembered the event from the Second World War and that's why he was killed. First he was beaten and died of his wounds. Did you hear anything about that? Anything to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard this before. I hear this from you the first time. He was accused of having been an Ustasha, that his ear was tattooed or branded, I don't know whether he was branded or tattooed. Actually, that this was under his left armpit. They wanted to take his clothes off to see whether that was true but he wouldn't let them do that. As far as I could see he was taken out and Zoks was the one who had beaten him the most. Although I was preoccupied with my own troubles, I would say that it seems to me that he even kicked him in the corner of the room and then took him out. What happened outside, we heard screams and shouts, but we don't know what happened. In addition to that group that comprised Cele, Pufta, as well as Zoks, there was another group, Niski came. I could not see outside, I don't know what was happening outside. We only heard kicks and thuds and then he crawled into the room and I only know that he said, "I am dying here, children. Pray for me."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the -- of this village Trsic around Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not there. I know that it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't know about the Popovic property where Vojo Camic and Nikola Zekic were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then I won't insist on that. This is the information that I received from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that information because I never heard this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not insisting. I appreciate that you maybe don't know anything about that. I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, tell me the time. I think you just about have used up your time, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may put just one more question while this is being checked. I think I have another minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, ask your last question. You've used up three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you were arrested and taken to prison, and you spent more than a few months there, you were arrested by a Muslim who belonged to a Serb military formation; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He belonged to the reserve police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Together with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, together with them, they kept guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I just wanted you to confirm this because obviously there were Muslims in the Serb formations as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just provide a comment to this? At the time before the conflict broke out in Zvornik, there were joint guards preventing gangs from storming into town. There was still no conflicts happening and I suppose that was the reason why they were joint guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have a redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I just have one short question for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to the looting, indeed in the indictment, there is a mention made of looting including in Zvornik. I listened to you carefully. You explained that you would go into Muslim houses and into Serb houses and I also seem to understand you gave an example that there was a factory out of which all of the equipment had been removed and had been loaded on to a truck. Did I misunderstand you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a crafts shop in Hrid near to the main road. That person was a tinsmith, and I believe that he had patented making grills or barbecues for something that was considered a national specialty in the former Yugoslavia, cevapcici and hamburgers. We loaded all those grills with -- and we put some roof tiles over those grills and even some machinery. I believe that we loaded those on Ljubisa's truck. He was from Loznicka Polje. I'm not sure that it was his truck but I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just a follow-up question. When all this equipment would be loaded on to the trucks, were there JNA military in the streets or were there only, say, Arkan's men or other people there? Because I was listening carefully to what you say about the takeover the Zvornik, you mentioned tanks. So one could infer from that that there was a military operation going on. Once the town was taken, did the JNA people go? What can you say about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did see the troops in town but in small numbers. But a majority of the mobilised soldiers were either on the lines or in the barracks and one could see those formations in town and from the moment we started loading things in town at the beginning of June or the end of May when Toro, Zoks, and the others had taken over, they were the only ones who went with us. The troops would come by or the police would come by to take control. They had a paper that they would open. The police would then read the paper and then they would move on. I suppose they had the authority to do all that and we did see the regular police around town but not on every corner. But I wouldn't say that there was a unit billeted in town or deployed in town. We didn't see them. There was the police and these military formations which are not regular army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are therefore telling me that there was a regular army in town but they were not many people or that the army people were not numerous. But did you see soldiers around -- or military police around in town, you can identify them because they've got this white belt showing that they are military police members. Did you see any MPs around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw all of them on the street but not in large numbers. It didn't look like a unit had been brought town. There were patrols, military, the police patrols and there are always people around the old bridge in Zvornik, you could see a lot of people wearing uniforms there. But those were very colourful uniforms, some wore camouflage uniforms, some had olive drab uniforms, some had insignia, the others didn't. So it was very difficult to tell who they were. There were all sorts of troops around the town but not in large numbers. You could not see large groups standing in one place. The most you could see were some five to ten standing around the bridge, that was the most that we could see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One very last question. When you would load things on to the trucks, and we know that you had a damaged arm so you couldn't load up everything, could you not have escaped? Because everybody was busy putting things, equipment into the trucks or counting the bank notes, wasn't it possible for you to flee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1013 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was scared, first of all. Second of all, luckily enough, I had grown up in town, I was not familiar with the ground around the town. I did try to escape towards Tuzla which fell through and I hoped that if I did my job properly, that my life would be saved. That was my hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you have now finished your testimony. On behalf of my colleagues and myself, we thank you for coming to testify. We know that you suffered. You described the blows you took and rest assured that you have everybody's sympathy including the sympathy of the accused who also expressed his own views regarding your ordeal. So all we can do is encourage you to continue in your current occupation and wish you a safe return home. Before you leave the courtroom, we'll have to lower the blinds. We still have a few minutes so we can do that and you'll have time to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that you as a Trial Chamber, together with all the people in the world will make sure that nobody, not even my worst enemy ever experiences what I went through during the war. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Please leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into closed session. Closed session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in open session, the hearing stands adjourned. We shall reconvene tomorrow at 8.30. Thank you.
